355.title: The Circle Spinout Nobody Googles
355.text: OpenTrade was spun out from Circle, which is why its vault contracts run on Circle's own open-source Perimeter Protocol — an origin that lends credibility and implies institutional DNA without requiring Circle's blessing. XMMF holds Fidelity's USD Money Market Fund through a Cayman SPC with J.P. Morgan as both custodian and broker, which is institutional plumbing worthy of a product ten times its $39 million size. Avalanche hosts roughly three-quarters of supply, an unusual distribution for an EVM-native product, explained by early partnerships with Avalanche-native institutional DeFi integrations. With no CoinGecko listing and no DefiLlama stablecoin coverage, XMMF exists almost entirely within the authenticated OpenTrade dashboard and a handful of Avalanche protocols — the tokenized equivalent of a well-run operation that has no particular interest in being discovered.

usdt-tether.title: Too Big to Depeg
usdt-tether.text: Tether commands more stablecoin market cap than the next four competitors combined, backed by a reserve that is 92% U.S. Treasuries and reverse repos — a composition that would have seemed implausible five years ago. Deployed natively across 28 chains with the deepest DEX liquidity of any stablecoin, USDT's infrastructure moat runs as deep as its capital reserves. The safety profile tells the expected story: near-perfect peg stability and overwhelming exit liquidity held back by a decentralization score that reflects what everyone knows — one company in El Salvador with freeze authority underwrites the world's most important dollar. Direct redemptions require a verified Tether account and a substantial minimum, so the peg for most holders is maintained by arbitrageurs rather than a personal right to redeem.

usdc-circle.title: The Compliance Premium
usdc-circle.text: Circle built the stablecoin that compliance departments approve on sight: 100% of reserves in very-low-risk assets — Treasuries, overnight repos, cash — managed by BlackRock and custodied at BNY Mellon, with institutional-top custody classification that even Tether doesn't match. Deployed across 41 chains with zero-fee direct redemptions, USDC's exit story is the cleanest in the market. The curious detail is that its peg score runs below Tether's, a residue of the March 2023 SVB weekend that still weighs on the tracking window despite years of near-perfect stability since. USDC's highest safety dimension is resilience — the one category where the quality of your custodian and regulator matters more than the size of your market cap.

dai-makerdao.title: The OG Decentralized Dollar
dai-makerdao.text: DAI is the stablecoin that proved crypto could create a dollar without a bank account, and seven years later it still earns the highest decentralization grade in the top ten — an A that reflects genuine DAO governance rather than a multisig cosplaying as one. The reserve composition has drifted far from crypto-purist origins: 40% U.S. Treasuries, 33% USDC through the PSM, with only a quarter in crypto collateral, making DAI functionally a hybrid fiat-crypto dollar. More depeg events on record than any other major stablecoin sounds alarming until you notice the peg score still sits in the high nineties, and the redemption backstop — atomic PSM access at zero fee — scores higher than almost everything else on the dashboard. Now overshadowed by its own rebrand as USDS, DAI occupies a strange position: the philosophical North Star of decentralized money, increasingly backed by the centralized assets it was designed to replace.

frax-frax.title: The Identity Crisis
frax-frax.text: Frax started life as crypto's boldest algorithmic experiment — a fractional-reserve stablecoin that actually worked — then abandoned the algorithm entirely in favor of tokenized treasuries. The reserve now reads like a TradFi allocation: 50% Superstate USTB, 42% BlackRock BUIDL, with the remainder in USCC and other tokenized assets, managed by a DAO that unanimously voted to trust BlackRock over its own math. The B+ in decentralization is the legacy of genuine DAO governance, but the C+ in dependency risk and 817 depeg events — more than almost any other stablecoin — reveal a turbulent history that no rebrand can erase. Trading well below peg with DEWS in the Watch band, legacy FRAX is slowly yielding to its successor frxUSD while the supply continues to contract.

tusd-trueusd.title: The Fallen Faithful
tusd-trueusd.text: TrueUSD was once positioned as the transparent alternative to Tether, but 99% of its reserves now sit in opaque First Digital Trust fund investments classified as very-high risk by Pharos — a reserve composition that inverts everything its name once promised. The Chainlink Proof of Reserve feed that prevents minting beyond attested reserves is a clever on-chain guardrail, but it can only verify quantity, not quality, of what First Digital Trust actually holds. Deployed across seven chains under a Dominica domicile with no meaningful regulator, TUSD persists as a cautionary tale about counterparty risk: the stablecoin still trades near peg, backed by assets whose actual composition remains opaque to the market. What started as a trust-minimized alternative now requires more trust in a single custodian than almost any other stablecoin on the dashboard.

lusd-liquity.title: Decentralization's Last Stand
lusd-liquity.text: LUSD earns an A- at 81 with perfect A+ scores in resilience, decentralization, and dependency risk — the only stablecoin backed 100% by ETH in immutable contracts with no governance keys, no admin functions, and no upstream dependencies. The 1,200 recorded depeg events and an A rather than A+ in peg stability reveal the trade-off: ETH-only collateral at 110% minimum creates a stablecoin that persistently trades above peg as borrowers maintain safety margins, currently sitting at +93 basis points. The 90-rated redemption backstop with permissionless atomic collateral redemption at 50 basis points provides the hard floor at $1, while the Stability Pool handles liquidations. Now overshadowed by its own successor BOLD with user-set interest rates and multi-collateral support, LUSD remains the philosophical benchmark against which every 'decentralized' stablecoin should be measured — the stablecoin that sacrificed market cap for principles and earned the highest resilience score on the dashboard for it.

mim-abracadabra.title: Scandal-Proof Somehow
mim-abracadabra.text: Multiple hacks, a founder whose Wonderland treasury manager was a convicted fraudster, a governance token down 99% from all-time high — yet MIM still trades near peg with a C safety grade and over 1,100 depeg events including one that cratered 7,500 basis points. The collateral is a museum of DeFi exotica: 35% yield-bearing vault tokens, 15% GMX V2 LP positions classified as very-high risk, alongside wstETH, WBTC, and other cauldron collateral spread across 14 chains. The peg score of 72 with only 89% time-at-peg tells you MIM lives in a persistent state of managed instability — borrowers buying discounted MIM to repay debt provides the reflexive peg mechanism, but it only works when borrowers exist and care about their positions. At this point, holding MIM requires less trust in the math and more faith in Daniele Sestagalli's ability to keep rebuilding after each crisis — a bet the market has been surprisingly willing to make for years.

usdp-paxos.title: The Quiet Regulator's Pet
usdp-paxos.text: Paxos's original stablecoin is the definition of doing everything right and getting ignored for it: 100% very-low-risk reserves in T-bills, overnight repos, and FDIC-insured cash, KPMG-audited under an OCC National Trust Charter, earning institutional-top custody and A+ across resilience and dependency risk. The C safety grade at 58 exposes the paradox: an F in liquidity with barely $270K in DEX TVL makes USDP one of the least liquid stablecoins relative to its regulatory pedigree, and the gap between institutional backing and on-chain presence is arguably the widest in the market. Paxos's real business is issuing stablecoins for others — PayPal's PYUSD, Paxos's USDG, formerly Binance's BUSD — making USDP less a product and more a proof of concept that Paxos can be trusted with your brand. Deployed on three chains with native multichain architecture, USDP exists primarily to demonstrate capabilities rather than to compete.

usdd-tron-dao-reserve.title: Justin Sun's Undying Dollar
usdd-tron-dao-reserve.text: USDD carries a D safety grade and a zero in decentralization — the literal floor — which is what happens when one person controls a stablecoin's governance and the reserve sits 75% in a Smart Allocator deploying stablecoins into Aave and JustLend DeFi strategies. The 329 depeg events and F in liquidity paint a grim picture, yet the PSM backstop scores an incongruous 95 — permissionless stablecoin swaps with 16% of supply available as immediate capacity, meaning the exit door is wider than the safety grade suggests. The reserves tell the real story: what was once an algorithmic stablecoin backed by Bitcoin is now mostly a DeFi yield strategy wrapped in a dollar token, with TRX comprising just 7% of backing. USDD persists on the TRON ecosystem's gravitational pull and Justin Sun's apparently inexhaustible appetite for financial experimentation, which is either a feature or a risk depending entirely on your priors about its founder.

dola-inverse-finance.title: The Comeback CDP
dola-inverse-finance.text: Inverse Finance lost $24M across two oracle manipulation exploits in 2022 and spent years clawing back — and the A+ in resilience is the vindication: a diversified collateral base of wstETH, cbBTC, ETH, and sUSDe powering FiRM's fixed-rate lending markets, with an 87-rated PSM backstop against USDS providing the peg floor. The 2,211 recorded depeg events and a peg score of 79 tell the other side of the story: DOLA has been below peg more often than almost any surviving stablecoin, though much of that history predates the protocol's restructuring. The sDOLA yield-bearing wrapper earns organic lending revenue from FiRM borrowers — the kind of unsexy, sustainable DeFi yield that rarely makes headlines but actually works. The B- overall grade reflects the tension between excellent collateral engineering and persistent peg fragility, with USDS as a mechanism-critical dependency that ties DOLA's fate to Sky's governance decisions.

gusd-gemini.title: The Ghost Dollar
gusd-gemini.text: Gemini Dollar was one of the first NYDFS-regulated stablecoins, and its reserve is still pristine: 62% T-bills and 38% cash at State Street, earning institutional-top custody and an A+ in both resilience and dependency risk. The ghost is in the liquidity: an F at 35 with barely $2 million in DEX TVL, where the DEX-implied price diverges from the primary by 750 basis points — the widest disconnect between on-chain reality and attested value of any top-tier-backed stablecoin. The C+ safety grade is a portrait of wasted potential: reserves that would earn an A from any institutional investor, trapped in a product that has lost the distribution war to USDC and PYUSD. GUSD is a museum piece — historically significant, technically sound, BPM-audited, and gathering dust on two chains while 2,400 recorded depeg events accumulate in its wake.

alusd-alchemix.title: Time Pays Your Debt
alusd-alchemix.text: Alchemix's self-repaying loans remain one of DeFi's most elegant ideas: deposit DAI, USDC, or USDT, borrow up to 50%, and let yield from Yearn and Aave strategies gradually erase your debt — no liquidations, no interest payments, just the slow passage of time converting future yield into present liquidity. The peg score of 46 and 1,390 depeg events tell the cost of elegance: alUSD persistently trades below peg because the self-repaying mechanism reduces the urgency of debt repayment that normally creates buying pressure, and the Transmuter's 1:1 redemption provides only a slow-drip floor. The exotic collateral quality classification is technically accurate but slightly unfair — the underlying assets are plain USDC and USDT deployed into audited lending protocols, not basis trades or exotic derivatives. alUSD is a stablecoin for patient DeFi users who've read the docs and accepted the trade-off: no liquidation risk in exchange for a peg that treats $1 as an aspiration rather than a guarantee.

susd-synthetix.title: The Longest Depeg
susd-synthetix.text: Synthetix's sUSD carries the only F/0 safety grade on the entire Pharos dashboard — the result of an active depeg that has persisted since SIP-420 slashed the collateralization ratio from 750% to 200% and forgave staker debt, with the token trading around $0.75 for months. The peg score of zero and over 3,000 recorded depeg events speak for themselves: the reflexive mechanism that maintained the peg for years — stakers buying discounted sUSD to repay their own debt — was structurally removed. The reserve tells the story of the transition: 50% SNX at very-high risk, 25% USDC via V3 Base pools, 15% ETH, and 10% in protocol treasury activity and SLP vault basis-trade strategies that are supposed to restore the peg by mid-2026. Whether the V3 transition and SLP vault can bring sUSD back from a 25% discount is the most consequential peg restoration attempt in DeFi history — and the warning notice on the dashboard suggests even the protocol isn't fully confident in the timeline.

ousd-origin-protocol.title: The Passive Yield Play
ousd-origin-protocol.text: Origin Dollar is 100% backed by USDC deployed into Morpho vaults (65%) and Curve AMO LP positions (35%), rebasing daily so your balance grows without staking or locking — the clever twist being that smart contracts must explicitly opt in to receive yield, so OUSD in non-opted AMM pools effectively subsidizes everyone else's returns. The 94-rated backstop with permissionless atomic stablecoin redemption at 0.25% fee is among the strongest of any yield-bearing stablecoin, providing a structural floor that the 181 depeg events have tested but never broken. The exotic collateral quality and wrapper governance classification reflect what OUSD actually is: a USDC yield strategy with a rebasing token wrapper, not an independent stablecoin with its own reserve management. A well-engineered product for the small cohort of users who want DeFi yield without the DeFi homework, on a shrinking market cap that suggests the cohort is indeed small.

cusd-celo.title: The Mobile-First Dollar
cusd-celo.text: Celo Dollar's reserve has evolved significantly from its crypto-heavy origins: 56% sUSDS (Sky's yield-bearing wrapper), 22% EURC, 12% CELO, and smaller positions in USDGLO, stETH, USDC, and ETH — a diversified basket at roughly 1.36x overcollateralization, maintained via the Mento AMM's oracle-driven arbitrage mechanism. The 1,571 depeg events and a peg score of 88 reflect the inherent volatility of an algorithmic stablecoin whose primary collateral includes both yield-bearing stablecoins and a native L1 token, though the DEWS Calm band at 5 suggests current conditions are stable. Deployed across five chains including Celo (now an Ethereum L2) and bridged to Ethereum, cUSD targets mobile payments in emerging markets where phone-number-based wallets matter more than DeFi composability. The German jurisdiction and self-reported reserve transparency at reserve.mento.org provide a governance anchor, but cUSD remains a niche stablecoin whose adoption depends on Celo's mobile-first thesis rather than on-chain DeFi demand.

eurc-circle.title: The Euro's Best On-Chain Bet
eurc-circle.text: Circle's EURC brings the same institutional-top custody and Deloitte attestations as USDC to the eurozone, backed 99% by deposits at systemically important European institutions — about as safe as euro reserves can get without being issued by the ECB itself. Licensed as an EMI by France's ACPR under MiCA, EURC is the regulatory benchmark that every other euro stablecoin is measured against, deployed across six chains including Ethereum, Base, Avalanche, and Solana. Euro stablecoins collectively represent a fraction of the global stablecoin market, making EURC both the dominant player in a small category and a reminder of how thoroughly the dollar owns this space. Circle's bet is that MiCA will eventually clear the field of unlicensed competitors, and that being the compliant survivor matters more than being the largest in a pre-regulatory free-for-all.

eurs-stasis.title: MiCA's Biggest Winner
eurs-stasis.text: Stasis Euro went from afterthought to contender because MiCA regulation cleared the field and EURS was already compliant — Malta MFSA licensed, BDO Malta audited, with 100% of reserves in euro balances at licensed European institutions including Central Bank accounts. The C- safety grade at 52 and active depeg trading over 800 basis points above its euro peg tell a more complicated story: 2,694 depeg events (712 in the four-year window) and a peg score of 38 make EURS one of the most frequently depegged stablecoins on the dashboard, with volatility that reflects both thin DEX liquidity and the challenge of maintaining an EUR peg against a dollar-denominated reference. The irony is that EURS's explosive growth happened not because the product changed, but because competitors got disqualified under MiCA. The looming threat is a consortium of European banks planning their own MiCA-compliant euro stablecoins, which would bring the kind of distribution and liquidity depth that Stasis cannot match.

ceur-celo.title: The Other Mento Euro
ceur-celo.text: Celo Euro shares the same Mento reserve as cUSD — 56% sUSDS, 22% EURC, 12% CELO, and smaller positions in various stablecoins and ETH — at approximately 136% overcollateralization, stabilized via the BiPoolManager virtual AMM with oracle-enforced EUR rates. The algorithmic classification and diversified reserve composition mean cEUR inherits both the strengths (on-chain transparency, overcollateralization) and weaknesses (crypto collateral volatility, thin secondary markets) of the Mento system. Deployed on Celo (now an Ethereum L2) with real-time on-chain reserve verification, cEUR exists primarily to serve Celo's vision of region-specific stablecoins for mobile payments rather than DeFi composability. In the euro stablecoin race dominated by Circle's EURC and MiCA-licensed competitors, cEUR's niche is geographic rather than regulatory.

eura-angle.title: Angle's DeFi Euro
eura-angle.text: Angle Protocol's EURA is one of the few crypto-backed euro stablecoins in a market dominated by RWA-backed MiCA-licensed issuers — an overcollateralized design with centralized-dependent governance that provides community involvement within practical guardrails. In the euro stablecoin race where Circle's EURC, SocGen's EURCV, and Banking Circle's EURI compete on regulatory credentials, EURA competes on DeFi composability and the absence of bank dependencies. For DeFi purists who want a euro without institutional custody chains, EURA is one of the few options on the menu, though the thin liquidity and modest market cap reflect the challenge of building a crypto-backed euro stablecoin when the regulated alternatives keep multiplying.

fpi-frax.title: Frax's Inflation Hedge
fpi-frax.text: Frax Price Index is pegged not to a currency but to the CPI-U — its redemption price grows on-chain per second at the 12-month U.S. inflation rate, updated monthly via Chainlink oracle, making it a stablecoin that preserves purchasing power rather than nominal value. Backed 100% by FRAX with AMOs generating yield to cover inflation accrual, FPI is classified as a wrapper with its entire dependency weight on legacy FRAX — meaning it inherits every risk in FRAX's own reserve stack of Superstate USTB and BlackRock BUIDL. The perfect peg score and zero depeg events reflect accurate CPI tracking rather than dollar stability, and the Ethereum-only deployment with no DEX liquidity data suggests FPI operates primarily as a philosophical product rather than a liquid trading instrument. The concept remains the most intellectually honest take on what 'stable' should mean — the execution is constrained by a wrapper dependency on a legacy stablecoin that is itself winding down.

uusd-youves.title: Tezos's Quiet Giant
uusd-youves.text: Youves' uUSD earns an F safety grade at 0 — trading at a 652-basis-point discount to peg with 2,154 depeg events and only 19% time at peg, making it alongside sUSD as the only other stablecoin to hit the absolute floor of the safety scale. The reserves — 60% XTZ, 20% USDt on Tezos, 10% tzBTC, and 10% SIRS LP tokens — with variable collateral ratios (200% for XTZ, 115% for stablecoins) are structurally sound, but the Tezos DeFi ecosystem has simply evaporated beneath the product. DEWS Alert at 44 confirms what the price shows: uUSD is in a persistent depeg state with no arbitrageurs willing to close the gap on a chain the broader market has stopped visiting. A functioning CDP stablecoin stranded on an island — the backing exists, but the market to value it does not.

lisusd-lista.title: BNB Chain's CDP Bet
lisusd-lista.text: Lista DAO's lisUSD transplants the MakerDAO CDP playbook to BNB Chain with a collateral mix that is 60% BNB ecosystem assets — 35% native BNB and 25% slisBNB (Lista's own LST) — plus 15% Binance-wrapped ETH and 10% BTCB, with a PSM accepting USDT, USDC, and FDUSD for peg stability. The 387 depeg events including one that cratered nearly 6,000 basis points below peg make lisUSD one of the most frequently depegged CDPs at scale, though the 85-rated PSM backstop with permissionless atomic settlement provides the structural floor. Deployed only on BSC with alt-LST collateral quality and no jurisdiction or proof of reserves disclosed, lisUSD's safety profile depends entirely on BNB's price stability and the PSM's capacity to absorb redemption pressure. Whether lisUSD can grow beyond Binance-subsidized adoption remains the central question — a CDP whose collateral and distribution both flow through a single ecosystem.

euroe-membrane.title: Paxos's EU Passport
euroe-membrane.text: EUROe started as a Finnish EMI-regulated euro stablecoin from Membrane Finance, KPMG-audited and quietly competent. Then Paxos acquired Membrane Finance specifically to gain MiCA compliance across 30 European countries — making EUROe less a standalone product and more Paxos's entry ticket to the EU market. Its future depends entirely on whether Paxos decides to scale EUROe as-is or rebrand it into its broader institutional stablecoin platform alongside USDP, PYUSD, and USDG. The acquisition playbook is familiar: buy a compliant shell, inherit the license, deploy institutional capital — a strategy that worked for Binance with BUSD until it didn't.

eure-monerium.title: Monerium's Electronic Money
eure-monerium.text: Monerium's EURe is one of the few stablecoins licensed as electronic money under MiCA, with 70% of reserves in a State Street AAA-rated EUR liquidity fund and 30% in bank deposits at Arion Bank and LHV Bank — institutional-top custody that earns an A+ in both resilience and dependency risk. The direct SEPA-to-IBAN integration makes fiat on/off-ramps seamless in a way most stablecoins only promise, and the eight-chain deployment across Ethereum, Polygon, Gnosis, and others gives EURe the broadest distribution of any euro stablecoin outside Circle's EURC. The C+ safety grade at 64 is dragged down by the F in decentralization and a D in liquidity — the persistent challenge of euro stablecoins that are well-backed but thinly traded. EURe is what euro stablecoins look like when they actually comply with European financial law — Iceland's FSA license may lack the prestige of France's ACPR, but the product is structurally sound.

eusd-electronic-usd.title: Reserve's Yield Basket
eusd-electronic-usd.text: Electronic USD is a Reserve Protocol stablecoin backed by a basket of yield-bearing USDC and USDT positions — 33% Compound V3 USDC, 33% Aave V3 USDC, and 34% Compound V3 USDT — with RSR stakers providing first-loss overcollateralization. The C+ safety grade at 64 with A+ in both peg stability and resilience reflects the quality of the underlying lending positions, while the 85-rated backstop enables permissionless 1:1 redemption against the collateral basket with automatic rebalancing via Dutch auctions. The 327 depeg events including one that hit 1,322 basis points below peg reveal the volatility of the basket's secondary market, though the 168-day peg streak suggests the mechanism has matured since its rocky early period. Supply is contracting at double digits monthly — an orderly wind-down from a product that found structural soundness but not adoption momentum.

crvusd-curve.title: Curve's Own Medicine
crvusd-curve.text: When the protocol that handles more stablecoin volume than anyone else launches its own stablecoin, the design had better be interesting — and crvUSD delivers with LLAMMA, which replaces hard liquidations with gradual rebalancing through price bands, letting collateral be automatically rebought if prices recover. The reserve is 69% WBTC/cbBTC and 11% tBTC with the rest in ETH derivatives, making crvUSD the most BTC-heavy CDP stablecoin at scale — though that BTC custody runs through BitGo and Coinbase, introducing the centralized dependencies that crypto-native collateral was supposed to avoid. Four PegKeeper pools paired with USDC, USDT, PYUSD, and frxUSD maintain the peg, while DAO governance and nine-chain deployment via canonical bridges keep the decentralization grade credible. The savings vault scrvUSD creates a self-correcting feedback loop where depeg pressure increases yields and attracts buyers back — elegant game theory from the team that understands AMM dynamics better than anyone, deployed on a collateral base that contradicts its crypto-native aspirations.

gho-aave.title: Aave's Dollar, Grown Up
gho-aave.text: GHO earns an A- safety grade — the highest of any DeFi-native stablecoin on the dashboard — backed by a diversified collateral base of wstETH, ETH, sDAI, and WBTC drawn from Aave V3's battle-tested lending pools. The redemption backstop is the standout: a 99 score with high confidence, powered by GSM stability modules offering permissionless swaps at single-digit basis-point fees with 40% of total supply available as immediate capacity. The 194 depeg events sound alarming but reflect GHO's rocky post-launch period in 2023; the peg has since stabilized through the GSM mechanism that makes depegs self-correcting by creating arbitrage opportunities. The B+ in decentralization reflects genuine DAO governance — Aave's multibillion-dollar protocol governs GHO's facilitator caps and risk parameters — though the dependency on sDAI means GHO partially inherits whatever Sky/MakerDAO decides to do with its own reserves.

fdusd-first-digital.title: Binance's Current Favorite
fdusd-first-digital.text: First Digital USD rose to prominence as Binance's preferred stablecoin after BUSD's regulatory demise, and its reserves are genuinely clean: 74% T-bills, 18% cash, and the rest in bank deposits and overnight repos — all very-low risk, attested by IAPA International and Prism. The connection to First Digital Trust — the same custodian whose opaque fund investments make TUSD's reserves a red flag — is the uncomfortable shared lineage, though FDUSD's own reserve composition is transparent and conventional. Deployed across six chains including Sui, TON, and Solana alongside the expected EVM networks, the distribution follows Binance's ecosystem preferences more than organic DeFi demand. FDUSD's fate remains a single-dependency story: Binance's endorsement made it, and Binance's pivot to another preferred stablecoin could unmake it just as quickly.

pyusd-paypal.title: The Fintech Giant's Dollar
pyusd-paypal.text: PayPal's PYUSD has quietly grown into a top-ten stablecoin — proof that when a company with 400 million accounts issues a dollar token, scale eventually follows. The reserve structure is almost comically conservative: 97% in Treasury reverse repos with the balance in cash, custodied at institutional-top tier under Paxos's OCC national trust charter, earning a resilience grade that puts it alongside USDC and ahead of Tether. Zero-fee redemption through Paxos and a near-perfect peg score make the product technically unimpeachable. The tension is distribution: five chains, modest DeFi integration, and a DEX footprint concentrated on just three networks suggest PYUSD is still the best-credentialed stablecoin that hasn't decided whether its future is on-chain or inside PayPal's own walls.

gyen-gyen.title: The Yen's Only Option
gyen-gyen.text: GYEN is issued by GMO Trust under a NYDFS trust charter with 100% of reserves in JPY at FDIC-insured institutions or short-dated T-bills, attested by The Network Firm — institutional-regulated custody and the only JPY stablecoin with genuine US regulatory credentials. The market for a yen stablecoin is inherently niche: Japan's own regulatory framework remains restrictive, the JPY's persistent weakness against the dollar limits demand from non-Japanese users, and JPYC's domestic FSA license covers the Japanese market directly. Deployed on just two chains, GYEN's value proposition is less about competing with dollar stablecoins and more about being the credible digital yen that's available outside Japan's domestic regulatory perimeter. The NYDFS charter is both its strength and its limitation — the most regulated JPY token on the market, regulated in a country that doesn't use yen.

usdy-ondo-finance.title: Ondo's Yield Machine
usdy-ondo-finance.text: Ondo's USDY offers tokenized U.S. Treasury exposure across 14 chains to everyone outside the United States — the irony of democratizing American government debt by excluding American persons remains the product's defining contradiction. Backed entirely by very-low-risk assets with Ankura Trust real-time attestations, the product is structurally sound but earns only a C+ safety grade — dragged down by an F in decentralization and a D in liquidity that reflects thin DEX pools relative to its billion-dollar-plus circulation. As a NAV-appreciating token rather than a pegged stablecoin, USDY has never depegged because it was never designed to hold a fixed price, which makes its presence on a stablecoin dashboard a philosophical question the market has answered with its wallet. The 14-chain deployment is the broadest of any tokenized treasury product, suggesting Ondo is building for distribution scale that its competitors haven't yet attempted.

cadc-cad-coin.title: Canada's Lonely Loonie
cadc-cad-coin.text: CADC is backed 100% by CAD and liquid securities (sub-90-day maturity) in a segregated trust, registered with FINTRAC as an MSB (C10001420) under the Loon brand, with institutional-regulated custody and self-reported reserve transparency via a Dune dashboard. Deployed across four chains including Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Base, CADC has broader EVM reach than most local-currency stablecoins despite its modest scale. The Canadian stablecoin market remains wide open — the Bank of Canada has urged federal regulation but Parliament hasn't acted — and CADC's bet is that being the first compliant CAD stablecoin matters more than being the biggest. Whether first-mover advantage in a market waiting for regulatory clarity is a position of strength or a position of uncertainty depends on how fast Ottawa moves.

usde-ethena.title: The Basis Trade, Tokenized
usde-ethena.text: Ethena's USDe pioneered the delta-neutral stablecoin and became crypto's third-largest — then quietly restructured its backing so that 76% of collateral now sits in liquid stablecoins, primarily its own USDtb backed by BlackRock's BUIDL. The remaining quarter runs the original playbook: spot BTC and ETH hedged with CEX perpetual shorts, custodied off-exchange through Ceffu and Copper. The safety profile reveals the structural tension: a near-perfect peg score paired with an F in resilience, reflecting exotic collateral quality and CEX-tier custody that no amount of funding-rate alpha can paper over. The dependency chain runs three layers deep — USDe depends on USDtb, which depends on BUIDL — making Ethena's synthetic dollar ultimately backstopped by BlackRock's tokenized money market fund, which would surprise most of its holders.

aeur-anchored-coins.title: The Swiss Euro, Winding Down
aeur-anchored-coins.text: Anchored Coins' AEUR is in terminal decline: FlowBank SA, which held 15% of AEUR's euro reserves, declared bankruptcy in June 2024, locking a portion of collateral in proceedings. Anchored Coins has ceased new issuance and was delisted from Binance EEA in March 2025, leaving 85% of reserves at Swissquote Bank SA intact but the product functionally winding down. The peg score of 29 and 216 depeg events including one that spiked over 8,400 basis points reflect the chaos of a stablecoin whose reserve partner failed. AEUR is now less a competitive euro stablecoin and more a cautionary tale about single-custodian concentration risk — the kind of counterparty failure that every stablecoin investor assumes won't happen until it does.

buck-bucket-protocol.title: Sui's CDP Experiment
buck-bucket-protocol.text: Bucket Protocol brings the MakerDAO playbook to Sui: deposit SUI (45%), USDC/USDT via PSM (25%), wrapped BTC (15%), or ETH/LSTs (15%), mint BUCK at zero interest, get liquidated at 110% collateral ratio. The 90-rated backstop with direct BUCK redemption for collateral provides a strong structural floor, but the 553 depeg events including one that cratered 7,505 basis points below peg reveal what happens when the primary collateral is a volatile L1 token. The F in decentralization at 15 reflects the established-alt-L1 chain penalty, and the PSM module accepting USDC and USDT is a polite way of saying the decentralized stablecoin ultimately leans on centralized ones when it matters. A DEWS score of 2 — among the lowest on the dashboard — suggests the current period is unusually calm for a product whose history includes some of the most severe depegs of any surviving CDP.

vchf-vnx.title: The Swiss Franc, Tokenized
vchf-vnx.text: VNX's VCHF is backed 100% by CHF deposits at Swiss and Liechtenstein banks, AREVA audited under Liechtenstein's FMA TVTG/Blockchain Act, with institutional-regulated custody and deployment across five chains including Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche, and Solana. For the small audience that specifically needs a regulated Swiss franc token on-chain, VCHF is one of the only options alongside Frankencoin's decentralized ZCHF — two very different philosophical approaches to the same currency. The five-chain deployment is more infrastructure than current demand warrants, suggesting VNX is building for a future where CHF on-chain liquidity matters more than it does today. VCHF is less a liquid trading instrument and more a regulated proof-of-concept that CHF can exist on-chain with genuine compliance infrastructure.

veur-vnx.title: Liechtenstein's Quiet Euro
veur-vnx.text: VNX's VEUR is backed 100% by euro cash and equivalents with AREVA attestations under Liechtenstein's FMA Blockchain Act license, deployed across an impressive 11 chains including Ethereum, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Solana, XRPL, Tezos, and ICP — the broadest distribution of any euro stablecoin on the dashboard. The institutional-regulated custody and FMA oversight provide genuine regulatory substance, but VEUR is dwarfed by Circle's EURC and the MiCA-compliant competition from SocGen, Banking Circle, and Quantoz. Eleven chains is ambitious distribution for a token that very few people are currently moving, suggesting VNX is building infrastructure for a multi-chain euro liquidity layer that the market hasn't demanded yet. The Liechtenstein FMA license is respected but carries less weight than France's ACPR or the Netherlands' DNB in the MiCA hierarchy.

audd-novatti.title: Australia's Dollar On-Chain
audd-novatti.text: AUDD is backed 100% by AUD cash and Treasury bills at Authorised Deposit-taking Institutions, issued by AUDC Pty Ltd under AFSL No. 700123 (a Novatti subsidiary listed on the ASX), with monthly independent reserve attestations by William Buck. The ASIC regulatory framework and institutional-regulated custody give AUDD genuine compliance credibility in a market where most non-USD stablecoins operate with minimal oversight. Selection for the Reserve Bank of Australia's Project Acacia testing tokenized asset settlement adds central bank validation that no other AUD stablecoin can claim. Deployed on three chains, AUDD is quietly answering whether Australia's stablecoin market can sustain a domestic alternative to USD-denominated tokens — a question whose answer depends more on Australian DeFi adoption than on the quality of the product itself.

cgusd-cygnus-finance.title: Base's Treasury Wrapper
cgusd-cygnus-finance.text: Cygnus Finance's cgUSD rebases daily on New York banking days to reflect its portfolio NAV — 80% off-chain T-bills with 15% in on-chain USDC/USDT and 5% accrued interest — and a Transmuter enables instant 1:1 conversion to USDC for holders who need immediate exit. The 422 depeg events and a worst deviation of nearly 2,800 basis points below peg tell a different story than the clean treasury-wrapper pitch: the gap between off-chain NAV and on-chain price creates persistent arbitrage friction that the rebase mechanism doesn't fully close. Institutional-unregulated custody with no published jurisdiction or proof of reserves means the trust assumptions sit entirely with the Cygnus team. Base-only deployment is a pragmatic choice for a chain that hosts USDC's issuer, but the peg score of 77 and 5-7 day settlement windows for non-Transmuter withdrawals suggest cgUSD's convenience premium is narrower than it appears.

fxusd-f-x-protocol.title: A CDP With Extra Steps
fxusd-f-x-protocol.text: f(x) Protocol's fxUSD is a CDP stablecoin backed 58% by WBTC and 42% by wstETH, with an 89-rated redemption backstop that makes it one of the best-backstopped DeFi stablecoins — the Stability Pool arbitrages the USDC/fxUSD Curve pool to defend the peg, offering wstETH real yield, fxSAVE autocompound, or FXN gauge rewards. The B- safety grade at 66 reflects a clean profile: A+ peg stability, A- resilience from the OpenZeppelin-audited overcollateralized design, and a DEWS score of 10 in the Calm band. The xPOSITION NFTs represent looped leveraged positions up to 10x — standard CDP dynamics where if leverage demand drops, fxUSD supply contracts naturally without threatening the peg. Ethereum-only deployment with $10.6M in DEX TVL keeps fxUSD niche, but the collateral quality and backstop mechanics put it among the better-engineered CDPs on the dashboard.

usdb-blast.title: Blast's Yield Mirage
usdb-blast.text: USDB is Blast L2's auto-rebasing dollar token — 60% backed by DAI/sDAI earning Maker's DSR yield, with 25% USDC and 15% USDT rounding out the reserve. The 1,329 depeg events and a peg score of 66 with only 87% time-at-peg tell the story of a stablecoin whose rebasing mechanics create constant micro-deviations that the market struggles to arbitrage on a chain with diminishing attention. The A+ in resilience at 88 reflects the quality of the underlying stablecoin collateral, but the F in liquidity at 36 with barely $1.5 million in DEX TVL on a single chain confirms what everyone suspected: Blast's TVL collapsed after the airdrop farming ended, and USDB's technically sound yield mechanics now run on a chain the market has largely moved on from. The yield at under 1% APY — well below the T-bill rate — is the final indignity for a product that was supposed to make holding dollars productive.

buidl-blackrock.title: The Institutional Monolith
buidl-blackrock.text: BlackRock's BUIDL has quietly become the largest tokenized money market fund, backed by T-bills and repos at BNY Mellon with institutional-top custody — and it earns only a B- safety grade, which tells you everything about what Pharos measures versus what a brand name implies. The perfect peg score and A+ resilience are expected from the world's largest asset manager; the F in decentralization and complete absence of DEX liquidity are equally expected from a product restricted to Reg D qualified purchasers. BUIDL's real significance is as infrastructure rather than a tradeable asset: it sits inside the reserve stacks of USDe, USDtb, frxUSD, USD0, and a growing list of stablecoins that want T-bill backing without managing the compliance themselves. Eight chain deployments via Securitize are expanding the footprint, but BUIDL remains the stablecoin that other stablecoins hold — not the one retail users ever touch.

btcusd-btcfi.title: Bitcoin's CDP Outpost
btcusd-btcfi.text: BtcUSD is backed 100% by overcollateralized Bitcoin in various wrapped forms — WBTC, BTCB, cbBTC, and native BTC — with alt-LST collateral quality classification reflecting the custody chains each wrapper adds. The peg score of 64 and over 1,000 depeg events including one that hit nearly 1,400 basis points make it one of the most frequently depegged CDPs per unit of market cap, though the DEWS Calm band at 15 suggests current conditions are stable. Deployed on Base and Bifrost with no modeled redemption backstop, the exit routes are limited to secondary market trading on chains the broader DeFi market doesn't heavily visit. The question remains whether BTC holders will trust yet another wrapping layer when established CDPs already accept wrapped Bitcoin with better liquidity and peg infrastructure.

usbd-bima.title: Bitcoin Wrappers, Dollar Ambition
usbd-bima.text: Bima's USBD is backed 100% by Bitcoin LSTs, LRTs, and approved BTC wrappers in Liquity-style vaults at 150% minimum collateral ratio, with permissionless redemption at $1 of BTC-denominated collateral and a Peg Stability Module adding near-1:1 USDC/USDP/GUSD swaps. The DAO governance classification and on-chain custody are structurally sound, but the alt-LST collateral quality and DEWS Alert band at 38 reflect the reality that 'Bitcoin-backed' here means a stack of counterparties around Bitcoin, not plain BTC. Deployed across five chains including Hemi, Plume, and Sonic alongside Ethereum and BSC, the distribution targets emerging ecosystems where established CDPs haven't arrived. The catch remains that every wrapper and bridge in the BTC custody chain adds a failure point that the Liquity-style redemption mechanics can't eliminate.

gyd-gyroscope.title: The All-Weather Dollar
gyd-gyroscope.text: Gyroscope's GYD is an exercise in paranoid stablecoin design: a diversified reserve of 40% sDAI, 30% USDC, 15% LUSD, and 15% crvUSD, with a primary-market AMM that algorithmically adjusts redemption prices during crises to preserve solvency. The 83-rated backstop and A in resilience validate the engineering, but the DEWS Alert band and a DEX-implied price that diverges over 1,500 basis points from the primary feed tell a more complicated story — the circuit-breaker mechanism that prevents bank runs also creates pricing dislocations that the secondary market struggles to arbitrage. The 110 depeg events and four dependencies on other stablecoins (sDAI, USDC, LUSD, crvUSD) mean GYD's all-weather thesis is only as strong as the least stable coin in its basket. The design optimizes for surviving tail risks rather than maximizing yield — noble engineering that has yet to convince the market to trade it at par.

isc-international-stable-currency.title: The Anti-Dollar Experiment
isc-international-stable-currency.text: ISC deliberately rejects the USD peg in favor of tracking purchasing power through a basket of gold, bonds, T-bills, equities, and cash — a flatcoin that appreciates over time rather than losing value to inflation, with NAV-based pricing and a 20% USDC dependency noted in its reserve structure. The institutional-unregulated custody and Solana-only deployment place ISC firmly in experimental territory, and the variable peg currency classification makes it harder to use as a medium of exchange than a conventional dollar token. As a concept, ISC is the most intellectually honest take on what 'stable' should mean — stable purchasing power rather than stable nominal value. At minimal market cap, ISC is about as niche as stablecoins get, proving that being philosophically right and being commercially viable are different things.

usd0-usual.title: The Usual Suspect
usd0-usual.text: Usual's USD0 is a stablecoin backed by stablecoins backed by stablecoins: 65% Hashnote USYC, 15% M by M0, 10% Ethena's USDtb, 5% BlackRock BUIDL, 3% Ondo's OUSG, and 2% Circle's USDC — six distinct upstream dependencies, each carrying its own counterparty chain down to the actual Treasury bills. The C- in dependency risk is the inevitable consequence of this architecture: every wrapper adds a layer, and USD0 has more layers than most buildings. The December 2024 USD0++ depeg remains the cautionary asterisk — a reminder that innovative tokenomics around the USUAL governance token can destabilize what the reserve composition was designed to protect. The 86-rated redemption backstop via permissionless DaoCollateral swaps is the structural safeguard, but with 38 depeg events and DEWS in the Watch band, USD0 demands more trust in its dependency stack than most holders probably realize.

usr-resolv.title: The Insured Basis Trade
usr-resolv.text: Resolv's USR runs the delta-neutral playbook — long ETH and BTC spot, short perpetual futures — but introduces a structural innovation that Ethena lacks: the RLP insurance layer, a dedicated pool of surplus collateral that absorbs negative funding rates and liquidation losses before they touch USR holders. The reserve split is 55% ETH/wstETH and 20% BTC hedged with CEX perps on Binance, Hyperliquid, and Deribit, with Fireblocks handling off-exchange custody and Apostro providing real-time reserve verification. Deployed across seven chains with exotic collateral quality classification, USR competes directly with USDe for the delta-neutral dollar market by betting that explicit risk separation — yield-seeking capital in RLP, stability-seeking capital in USR — is more honest than an opaque insurance fund. Whether the insurance layer can survive a prolonged negative funding regime remains untested at scale, but the architecture is the most transparent attempt to solve the basis trade's known failure mode.

usdz-anzen.title: Private Credit Meets DeFi
usdz-anzen.text: Anzen's USDz is 80% backed by U.S. private credit ABS — SMB merchant receivables, factored invoices, auto leases, consumer installment lending, and litigation finance — underwritten by SEC-licensed broker-dealer Percent, with 15% in Superstate tokenized treasuries and 5% cash. The 559 depeg events and a peg score of 48 make USDz one of the most frequently depegged stablecoins on the dashboard, and supply has collapsed over 80% in a single month, answering the question of what happens when holders lose confidence in private credit backing. Qualified Market Makers mint at 1:1 USDz/USDC while retail relies on DEX arbitrage to close the gap — a two-tier system that works when the market trusts the collateral and breaks when it doesn't. The yield from private credit is real and uncorrelated with crypto markets, but so is the liquidity mismatch between 90-day receivables and instant redemption expectations.

ausd-agora.title: The VanEck-Managed Dollar
ausd-agora.text: Agora's AUSD has the resume that makes compliance departments swoon: VanEck manages the reserves, State Street provides custody in a bankruptcy-remote Delaware Statutory Trust, and Chaos Labs delivers real-time proof of reserves on-chain — institutional-top custody that earns an A+ in resilience alongside near-perfect peg stability. The 14-chain deployment including emerging networks alongside the expected EVM chains is an aggressive distribution play that gives AUSD broader reach than most competitors twice its size. The revenue-sharing model with distribution partners — where Agora splits reserve yield with platforms that drive adoption — is the closest thing to a structurally aligned growth flywheel in the stablecoin market. With a DEWS score of just 2 and only 18 depeg events on record, AUSD is one of the least stressed stablecoins on the dashboard, held back only by the F in decentralization that every centralized issuer earns by default.

usds-sky.title: The Endgame Dollar
usds-sky.text: Sky Dollar is MakerDAO rebranded, but the numbers tell a story the name change cannot: supply has surged to make USDS one of the largest stablecoins in existence, driven by the same PSM and vault architecture that sustained DAI for years. The reserve mix — 40% U.S. Treasuries, 30% USDC through the PSM, 20% ETH — earns a balanced B+ across every safety dimension, the most consistent scorecard in the top ten. The redemption backstop is the real headline: permissionless atomic PSM swaps with roughly a third of total supply available as immediate capacity at zero fee, giving USDS arguably the best exit infrastructure of any stablecoin at scale. The dependency on Circle's USDC as mechanism-critical collateral is the one contradiction a DAO-governed stablecoin probably wishes it could resolve.

m-m0.title: The Middleware Dollar
m-m0.text: M0's M token is backed 100% by short-term T-bills in bankruptcy-remote SPVs — a pristine reserve that earns a perfect peg score, yet the token trades persistently below peg with a D safety grade and a liquidity score of 5 out of 100. The disconnect between flawless backing and negligible on-chain liquidity is M0's defining paradox: this is infrastructure, not a consumer stablecoin. Permissioned Minters lock T-bill collateral while Validators cryptographically attest sufficiency on-chain — a novel trust architecture that replaces auditor attestations with protocol-level verification, at the cost of institutional-unregulated custody and no redemption backstop modeled by Pharos. M's significance is downstream: it powers Noble's USDN for Cosmos, MetaMask's mUSD, USD.AI's USDai, and Usual's USD0 — making M the stablecoin that nobody holds directly but everybody depends on.

usdm-moneta.title: Cardano's Dollar Anchor
usdm-moneta.text: Moneta's USDM is backed by 60% money market funds (Fidelity and Amundi for dual US/EEA issuance) and 40% USD bank deposits, with a Charli3 oracle verifying 1:1 reserve backing on-chain before each mint — a thoughtful guardrail that most stablecoins skip. The D safety grade at 45 with an F in peg stability seems harsh until you see the numbers: 1,656 depeg events and only 40% time at peg, making USDM one of the most frequently depegged stablecoins per unit of time despite clean fiat reserves. The Norwegian Finanstilsynet MiCA EMT license and institutional-regulated custody at established-alt-L1 chain tier provide genuine regulatory substance, but Cardano-only deployment limits the DeFi ecosystem to a fraction of what Ethereum offers. USDM proves once again that the hardest part of launching a stablecoin isn't the backing — it's building enough liquidity on the target chain to keep arbitrageurs interested in maintaining the peg.

satusd-river.title: The Purist's CDP
satusd-river.text: River's satUSD makes a deliberate choice: no centralized stablecoin collateral accepted, only BTC, ETH, BNB, and LSTs — a principled stance that earns an A+ in dependency risk but costs it a peg score in the sixties with over 200 depeg events including one that hit nearly 4,500 basis points. The Omni-CDP architecture lets users deposit collateral on one chain and mint satUSD on another via LayerZero, spreading across eleven chains including some classified as unproven — a deployment breadth that triggers decentralization penalties despite the protocol's genuinely decentralized governance as a Liquity V1 fork. The 88-rated redemption backstop offers permissionless atomic access to blue-chip collateral, but with minimal DEX liquidity across all chains, the secondary market is paper-thin. satUSD is the most ideologically pure CDP at scale, but purity and peg stability have proven to be competing objectives.

usdf-astherus.title: Binance's Shadow Dollar
usdf-astherus.text: Astherus USDF runs delta-neutral strategies exclusively through Binance via Ceffu's MirrorX infrastructure — 50% USDT backing with the other half split between spot crypto longs and perpetual short positions, all on a single exchange. The D safety grade and F in resilience tell the concentration story: CEX custody, exotic collateral quality, no published proof of reserves, and deployment on BSC alone with zero DEX liquidity, making it essentially invisible to on-chain analytics. The 86-rated stablecoin redemption backstop provides permissionless exit to USDT, but that exit depends on the same Binance infrastructure that holds the collateral — a single point of failure running through every layer of the stack. Supply has contracted sharply under the Aster DEX rebrand, suggesting holders are drawing their own conclusions about the risk-reward of a yield product whose entire existence is mediated by one exchange and one custodian.

usda-avalon.title: Bitcoin Banking, On-Chain
usda-avalon.text: Avalon's USDa is a BTC-collateralized CDP whose reserve tells a more nuanced story than the Bitcoin branding suggests: 45% FBTC (tokenized BTC via Cobo custody), 40% USDT minted 1:1, and 15% in assorted BTC LSTs including SolvBTC, LBTC, and pumpBTC — meaning the majority of backing is either a stablecoin or a wrapped version of Bitcoin with its own custody chain. The 1:1 USDT convertibility and institutional credit lines from Ceffu and Coinbase Prime provide the liquidity backstop, while a proprietary HFT liquidation engine runs on centralized exchange infrastructure rather than on-chain liquidation bots. Deployed across seven chains including Berachain, Movement, and Nibiru alongside the expected EVM networks, the distribution strategy targets emerging ecosystems where established CDP alternatives haven't yet arrived. USDa is structurally distinct from typical CDPs, but the alt-LST collateral quality classification and dependence on centralized custody infrastructure mean the Bitcoin-native narrative carries more counterparty risk than the branding implies.

usdtb-ethena.title: Ethena's Safe Side
usdtb-ethena.text: If USDe is Ethena's exciting sibling, USDtb is the responsible one — 90% backed by BlackRock's BUIDL with a 10% USDC buffer for fast redemptions, issued through Anchorage Digital under an OCC federal bank charter. The C safety grade looks harsh for a product whose underlying assets are almost entirely U.S. Treasuries, but the dependency score reveals the catch: USDtb inherits risk from both BUIDL and USDC, and its C in dependency reflects the chain of counterparties between a holder and the actual government bonds. USDtb's real purpose is less as a standalone stablecoin and more as the ballast inside USDe's reserve — 76% of Ethena's flagship product now sits in USDtb, making this the quiet load-bearing wall of a multibillion-dollar structure. On just three chains with modest DEX liquidity, USDtb is a product optimized for one customer: its own parent protocol.

zeusd-zoth.title: RWA Restaking's First Bet
zeusd-zoth.text: Zoth's ZeUSD earns an F safety grade at 38 despite a perfect peg score of 100 and zero depeg events — a paradox explained entirely by what surrounds the peg: institutional-unregulated custody in the Cayman Islands with no proof of reserves, an F in decentralization, and three weak dependencies on USYC, USD0, and M0 that each drag the dependency score below C-. The reserve is 70% tokenized T-bills (USYC, STBT, TBILL), 15% Usual's USD0++, and 15% wrapped M — a dependency chain where ZeUSD inherits risk from every upstream issuer in its RWA stack. The dual-yield model of off-chain T-bill interest plus on-chain restaking rewards targets returns above vanilla stablecoin staking, but the question is whether 'restaking your restaked treasury token' is financial innovation or unnecessary wrapper depth. The F grade is a warning that a perfect peg is necessary but not sufficient — the infrastructure around it matters just as much.

zchf-frankencoin.title: Swiss Stubbornness, Tokenized
zchf-frankencoin.text: Frankencoin is a genuinely decentralized Swiss franc stablecoin — no foundation, no team tokens, no VC backing — earning an A in decentralization that puts it alongside LUSD and BOLD in the tiny club of stablecoins with credible governance independence. The collateral is omnivorous: 45% wrapped BTC, 30% ETH derivatives, 10% gold tokens (PAXG, XAUT), 10% tokenized RWAs, and even CRV and GNO — all valued through oracle-free auction-based liquidation that avoids price feed manipulation at the cost of capital efficiency. The 502 depeg events and a peg score of 81 reflect the inherent challenge of maintaining a CHF peg against a dollar-denominated reference rate, amplified by thin DEX liquidity on eight chains. Frankencoin proves that small, well-designed protocols can survive without a marketing budget, though the B- safety grade acknowledges that ideological purity doesn't eliminate the liquidity constraints of a niche-currency stablecoin.

usn-noon.title: The Rotating Yield Engine
usn-noon.text: Noon's USN rotates between four yield sources based on market conditions: 40% USDC/USDT for liquidity, 30% T-bills for baseline yield, 20% delta-neutral funding-rate arbitrage for bull markets, and 10% CLOs and private credit for uncorrelated returns — the most diversified yield strategy of any delta-neutral stablecoin. The C safety grade at 59 reflects exotic collateral quality and modest DEX liquidity, but the DEWS score of 2 and 84-rated backstop with permissionless redemption suggest the product is operationally stable despite the complex reserve architecture. The 'intelligent allocation' pitch — acknowledging that no single yield source works in all market regimes — is a more honest framing than most competitors offer, verified by Accountable's real-time proof of solvency. The current 0% APY on sUSN is the awkward proof that honest yield reporting sometimes means reporting no yield at all, which is either transparency or a product without a pulse depending on your perspective.

honey-berachain.title: Berachain's Basket Dollar
honey-berachain.text: HONEY is Berachain's native stablecoin — a basket of 40% USDC, 25% USDT0, 20% pyUSD, and 15% USDe, minted into per-collateral vaults governed by BGT holders. The C- safety grade at 51 includes a zero in decentralization — the literal floor, triggered by Berachain's unproven chain classification and the -60 penalty it carries. The 85-rated redemption backstop and A in resilience tell the structural story: the basket design and per-vault architecture are sound, but deploying on a chain the market hasn't yet validated drags every safety dimension down. HONEY's fate is entirely coupled to Berachain's Proof-of-Liquidity model — if the chain attracts sustained TVL, HONEY thrives as the default dollar with its 15% USDe dependency as the main risk vector; if not, it's a well-designed wrapper on a chain nobody visits.

wusd-worldwide.title: The Payments Play
wusd-worldwide.text: WSPN's Worldwide USD is backed 55% by short-term T-bills and 40% by cash with a Basel III-inspired 6% liquidity buffer on non-cash reserves — a conservative structure that earns a perfect peg score of 100 with only two depeg events and a C+ safety grade at 60. The BVI domicile with FinCEN MSB registration and institutional-unregulated custody sits in an awkward regulatory middle ground, and the DEWS Watch band suggests the market sees stress signals the peg hasn't absorbed. Deployed on Ethereum, Polygon, and Viction with white-label infrastructure that lets enterprises issue their own branded stablecoins, WUSD targets trade finance and cross-border settlements rather than DeFi composability. The market cap remains modest despite partnerships spanning Philippines exchanges to Australian commodity exporters, suggesting the stablecoin payment network thesis is still more pitch deck than protocol.

frxusd-frax.title: Frax Grows Up
frxusd-frax.text: After years of algorithmic experimentation, Frax Finance went full TradFi with frxUSD — a stablecoin whose reserves are 55% BlackRock BUIDL, 20% Superstate USTB, and 10% Circle USDC, minted and redeemed 1:1 through governance-approved enshrined custodians that hold provable on-chain reserves. The 26-chain deployment is among the broadest of any non-USDC stablecoin, and the B+ in decentralization reflects genuine DAO governance over which custodians can mint — a structural advantage over purely centralized issuers. The C+ in dependency risk is the price of the strategy: frxUSD depends on BUIDL, USTB, USCC, and USDC, inheriting counterparty risk from every custodian in the chain. A near-400-day peg streak and institutional-top custody make frxUSD the most credible product Frax has ever shipped, though Sam Kazemian's stated ambition of applying for a Federal Reserve Master Account suggests the team considers BlackRock backing a stepping stone, not a destination.

usyc-hashnote.title: The Invisible Giant
usyc-hashnote.text: Hashnote's USYC has surged past $2 billion to become the largest tokenized Treasury product — and the most invisible, with zero DEX liquidity, a single-source price feed, and deployment on just two chains. The C+ safety grade on a product backed entirely by T-bills and reverse repos sounds paradoxical until you see the breakdown: an F in decentralization and the worst effective exit score of any top-ten stablecoin, reflecting the reality that exiting USYC means going through Hashnote's same-day redemption window, not a swap. As a NAV-appreciating token with a climbing price, USYC is less a stablecoin and more a tokenized money market fund — one that has grown explosively on institutional demand that apparently cares more about yield-to-maturity than on-chain exit routes. The Bermuda BMA license provides regulatory cover, but the absence of published proof of reserves is a pointed gap for a product of this scale.

eurr-stablr.title: Malta's Euro Bet
eurr-stablr.text: StablR's EURR is backed 100% by fiat euro at European financial institutions under a Malta MFSA EMI license with MiCA compliance and Grant Thornton attestations — the same regulatory infrastructure as its dollar sibling USDR, with Tether's strategic investment providing both capital and the awkward question of whether a Tether-backed entity can win institutional trust in a market built on regulatory purity. Ethereum-only deployment with institutional-regulated custody gives EURR clean infrastructure, but the euro stablecoin market remains a fraction of the dollar market, and competition from Circle's EURC, SocGen's EURCV, and Banking Circle's EURI means EURR must differentiate on something beyond compliance alone. The Tether connection is both asset and liability — distribution relationships and brand recognition offset by the regulatory scrutiny that follows Tether everywhere. Whether Malta's MFSA license carries the same weight as France's ACPR or the Netherlands' DNB in the MiCA credibility hierarchy remains the competitive question.

usdr-stablr.title: The Dollar Sibling
usdr-stablr.text: StablR's USDR rides the same Malta MFSA EMI license and MiCA compliance infrastructure as its euro sibling EURR, with 100% of reserves in cash and short-term government bonds at regulated European financial institutions, audited by Grant Thornton. The peg score of 96 sounds clean until the DEWS Alert band at 41 and recent depeg events — including one that hit over 1,000 basis points below peg — reveal severe pool imbalances with 91% stress on the worst pool and liquidity that contracted 67% in a single week. Ethereum-only deployment with the offchain-issuer redemption route capped by the route-family ceiling means the exit path runs through StablR's own API rather than on-chain arbitrage. A competent, regulation-first product in a market that increasingly rewards exactly that — but differentiating a compliant USD stablecoin at $6 million market cap in a field of dozens remains the core challenge.

usdo-openeden.title: Treasury Yield, Repackaged
usdo-openeden.text: OpenEden's USDO is a rebasing stablecoin fixed at $1 that distributes T-bill yield daily by increasing holder balances — backed 70% by OpenEden's own TBILL tokens, 15% by BlackRock BUIDL, 5% by Franklin Templeton BENJI, and 10% in USDC as a cash buffer. The Bermuda BMA DABA license and Chainlink Proof of Reserves provide regulatory and transparency layers that most rebasing stablecoins lack, though the peg score of 81 and 44 depeg events — including one that spiked nearly 17,000 basis points above peg — reveal the mechanical challenge of maintaining a $1 price on a token whose supply changes daily. The backstop scores a modest 52 with capacity issues, reflecting the illiquidity gap between holding tokenized treasuries and providing instant dollar redemptions. Deployed across four chains, USDO is elegant for retail but awkward for DeFi protocols that don't handle rebasing tokens — hence the cUSDO wrapper for composability.

usda-anzens.title: Cardano's Dollar, Finally
usda-anzens.text: Anzens USDA is backed 60% by USD cash deposits and 40% by U.S. Treasury securities, custodied by BitGo Trust under a FinCEN MSB license — a conventional, all-very-low-risk reserve for a Cardano-native stablecoin that the ecosystem has waited years to get. The C safety grade at 56 with a peg score of 55 and 605 depeg events tells the story of a stablecoin that arrived to a chain without enough DeFi depth to maintain consistent arbitrage, resulting in only 64% time at peg despite clean reserves. No tracked DEX liquidity and Cardano-only deployment mean USDA's exit routes are limited to direct redemption through Anzens via KYC-verified bank transfers. For a blockchain ecosystem long criticized for lacking stablecoin infrastructure, USDA is a necessary step — though the limited U.S. state availability and thin secondary market suggest the regulatory and liquidity paths are both far from complete.

usdf-falcon.title: Altcoin Alchemy
usdf-falcon.text: Falcon Finance runs the delta-neutral playbook with collateral that would make risk managers reach for antacids: 45% BTC shorts, 30% stablecoins, and — the part that distinguishes it from Ethena — 15% in altcoins including DOGE, FET, TRX, and TON, each hedged with perpetual shorts on centralized exchanges. It is the only top-ten stablecoin in the DEWS Watch band rather than Calm, and the only one persistently trading below peg, which together explain why a C+ safety grade accompanies over a billion dollars in circulation. The ht.digital real-time reserve transparency helps, but the fundamental question is whether delta-neutral strategies on altcoin perp markets — where liquidity can evaporate in hours — provide the same structural guarantee as the BTC and ETH hedges that defined the category. The yield on sUSDf is the carrot; the exotic collateral quality rating is the stick.

europ-schuman.title: France's MiCA Pioneer
europ-schuman.text: Schuman Financial's EUROP is built with the Banque de France's ACPR looking over its shoulder — 98% euro cash at Société Générale and other EU banks plus a 2% reserve buffer beyond the 1:1 requirement, KPMG-audited, with institutional-regulated custody that checks every box MiCA demands. Deployed across five chains including Ethereum, Polygon, Avalanche, XRPL, and Plasma, EUROP has broader multi-chain reach than most euro competitors despite its modest scale. The ACPR license from France's banking supervisor carries the same institutional weight as SocGen's own EURCV license, making EUROP one of the best-credentialed euro stablecoins in a market where credentials are table stakes. With euro stablecoins representing barely a fraction of the global stablecoin float, even the best-credentialed entrant faces a market that simply hasn't arrived yet.

brz-transfero.title: Latin America's Bridge
brz-transfero.text: BRZ gives Brazil's crypto traders a real-denominated on-ramp, and its thousands of depeg events — the most of any stablecoin on the dashboard by a wide margin — tell you everything about what happens when you peg a token to a currency as volatile as the Brazilian real against a dollar-denominated reference rate. Backed 100% by BRL cash at a Central Bank of Brazil-authorized institution with a Swiss VQF registration, the reserve is straightforward; the F in peg stability reflects FX volatility rather than reserve inadequacy. The DEX liquidity is vanishingly thin, and the 1% redemption fee through Transfero means the secondary market is the practical exit for most holders — a market with barely enough depth to absorb a single large order. BRZ serves a genuine need in one of crypto's largest retail markets, but the D safety grade is a reminder that non-USD stablecoins carry FX risk that no amount of institutional backing can eliminate.

rlusd-ripple.title: Ripple's Dollar Bet
rlusd-ripple.text: After years of fighting the SEC over XRP, Ripple obtained a NYDFS trust charter and launched a stablecoin with reserves that are 100% very-low-risk — T-bills, government money market funds, and cash — split evenly across asset types with BPM LLP attestations. The B safety grade reflects a clean balance sheet dragged down by the same D in decentralization that plagues every centralized issuer, but the 54 depeg events including one that hit 636 basis points reveal a rougher early history than the current steady peg suggests. RLUSD lives on just two chains — Ethereum and Ripple's own XRPL — a deliberate choice that prioritizes Ripple's cross-border payments corridor over DeFi ubiquity. The strategic question is whether a stablecoin designed for institutional settlement can compete for on-chain liquidity against issuers who have a five-year head start.

feusd-felix.title: Hyperliquid's Lending Layer
feusd-felix.text: Felix Protocol forked Liquity V2 and deployed it on Hyperliquid L1 with a collateral mix that is 60% HYPE ecosystem tokens (HYPE, kHYPE, wstHYPE) classified as very-high risk, alongside 15% BTC, 15% ETH, and 10% SOL. The 91-rated redemption backstop with fee-free permissionless collateral redemption is the highest backstop score of any stablecoin in this market cap range, providing a structural $1 floor that the 339 depeg events test regularly. The peg score of 88 and decentralized governance classification reflect the Liquity architecture's strengths, though the unproven chain tier penalty from Hyperliquid keeps the overall safety profile below what the mechanics deserve. feUSD exists to let Hyperliquid traders mint dollars against their HYPE positions for margin — a use case inseparable from the exchange's own momentum, making feUSD's fate a direct derivative of Hyperliquid's.

dusd-standx.title: Delta-Neutral via CeFi
dusd-standx.text: StandX's DUSD takes the Ethena playbook and runs it through Ceffu with the team's Binance Futures and Goldman Sachs pedigree explaining the institutional architecture. The F in resilience at 13 out of 100 is among the lowest scores on the dashboard, reflecting CEX custody, exotic collateral quality, no published proof of reserves, and a reserve that is 95% active trading positions with only a 5% stability buffer. The dependency on USDT and USDC as deposit assets means every dollar of backing passes through centralized exchange infrastructure before being deployed into hedged positions on two chains. With thin DEX liquidity and DEWS in the Watch band, DUSD is the delta-neutral stablecoin that most fully embraces CeFi risk — a bet that Goldman-trained quants can run funding-rate arbitrage better than anyone, if you trust the infrastructure not to fail.

eurcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SocGen's Blockchain Experiment
eurcv-societe-generale-forge.text: EUR CoinVertible is issued by SG-FORGE, the digital asset arm of a systemically important European bank, with reserves held 100% in euro cash at Société Générale itself — institutional-top custody that earns an A+ in both resilience and dependency risk, the highest marks available. The B- safety grade at 65 is dragged down by the F in decentralization and a liquidity score of 48 that reflects thin DEX pools relative to institutional backing, but the DEWS score of 1 — the lowest stress reading on the entire dashboard — suggests the product is operationally serene. Deployed across Ethereum, XRPL, Stellar, and Solana with MiCA EMI licensing from France's ACPR, EURCV is what happens when a 160-year-old bank decides to issue tokens on public blockchains. Whether this is the future of tokenized money or a corporate innovation lab's pet project depends on whether SocGen commits distribution resources that match its regulatory credentials.

yusd-aegis.title: Bitcoin-Margined Stability
yusd-aegis.text: Aegis's YUSD is 100% exposed to BTC — 50% spot held at Fireblocks, Copper, and Ceffu, with 50% in BTC-margined perpetual shorts — making the entire reserve an active trading position with exotic collateral quality and CEX custody. The D safety grade at 46 and F in resilience at 25 are the predictable consequence: when your entire backing is a delta-neutral strategy on a single volatile asset custodied at centralized exchanges, the safety floor is as thin as the funding rate is favorable. The real-time proof-of-reserves through Accountable is genuinely differentiated — you can watch custodial vaults and open positions in real time, which is more transparency than most competitors offer and exactly the transparency you need when the risk is this concentrated. The 84-rated stablecoin redemption backstop with permissionless exit provides a structural floor, but with thin DEX liquidity and DEWS in the Watch band, YUSD's survival depends on the same funding-rate dynamics that govern every delta-neutral stablecoin.

reusd-resupply.title: Curve's Recursive Dollar
reusd-resupply.text: Resupply's reUSD, built by the Convex and Yearn teams, is backed 60% by Curve Lend vault shares and 40% by Fraxlend vault shares — both classified as high-risk, making the entire reserve an active lending position rather than idle collateral. The 711 depeg events and a peg score of 53 are the predictable consequence of recursive leverage: deposit crvUSD into Curve Lend, use the position as collateral, mint reUSD, sell it for more crvUSD, repeat. The exotic collateral quality classification, Ethereum-only deployment, and absence of any backstop, proof of reserves, or disclosed jurisdiction mean reUSD operates with minimal safety infrastructure outside the protocol's own communal redemption mechanism with its 1% fee floor. The composability that pushed crvUSD to all-time-high supply is the same composability that makes reUSD fragile — a stablecoin whose stability is a derivative of two other stablecoins' lending markets.

tbill-openeden.title: The Original T-Bill Token
tbill-openeden.text: OpenEden's TBILL is a tokenized money market fund with 95% in short-dated U.S. Treasury bills managed by BNY Investments with institutional-top custody — earning an A+ in both resilience and dependency risk, the highest safety dimensions of any tokenized treasury product below BUIDL's scale. The B safety grade at 72 is constrained by the same F-adjacent decentralization score that plagues every centralized fund structure, but the perfect peg score and zero depeg events reflect what happens when your underlying asset is the world's safest security. As a NAV-appreciating token above $1, TBILL is less a stablecoin and more a regulated BVI fund that happens to be an ERC-20 — KYC-restricted to professional investors, which limits retail appeal but is precisely the point. Deployed on Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Solana, TBILL's real significance is as infrastructure: it appears in the collateral stacks of USDO and other OpenEden products that need T-bill exposure without managing BNY custody relationships themselves.

a7a5-old-vector.title: The Sanctioned Dollar's Mirror
a7a5-old-vector.text: A7A5 is a ruble-pegged stablecoin backed 100% by deposits at Promsvyazbank — a Russian state-owned bank under Western sanctions — which is why Pharos classifies its custody as institutional-sanctioned and its reserve risk as very-high despite the collateral being plain fiat currency. Issued by Old Vector LLC under a Kyrgyz VASP license with quarterly audits from an independent Kyrgyz firm, the regulatory architecture is technically compliant with its home jurisdiction while being functionally untouchable by Western financial infrastructure. The issuer distributes 50% of reserve interest to holders as additional A7A5, making it one of the few stablecoins that pays yield from a sanctioned bank's deposit rates. Whether A7A5 represents financial innovation for an isolated economy or sanctions evasion with a token wrapper depends entirely on whose compliance framework you're applying.

usd1-world-liberty-financial.title: The Presidential Stablecoin
usd1-world-liberty-financial.text: World Liberty Financial's USD1 arrived with the Trump family brand and proved that political controversy does not prevent a stablecoin from functioning: 100% very-low-risk reserves in T-bills, money market funds, and cash, custodied by BitGo under a South Dakota trust charter. The irony is structural — USD1 is, by the numbers, a perfectly conventional stablecoin with impeccable reserves and a near-perfect peg score, indistinguishable from any Paxos or Circle product except for the name on the letterhead. Supply has contracted by double digits recently, suggesting that the initial burst of politically motivated minting is unwinding as holders discover that USD1 earns no yield and has thinner DEX liquidity than competitors half its size. Whether the brand is an asset or a liability depends on which side of the political aisle you mint from, but the B safety grade suggests the product itself is unremarkable in the best possible way.

usdx-hex-trust.title: Hong Kong's Quiet Dollar
usdx-hex-trust.text: Hex Trust's USDX is backed 80% by T-bills and 20% by cash — a clean reserve composition that makes its F safety grade and active depeg all the more striking. Trading nearly 500 basis points below peg with 842 depeg events and the worst reaching over 7,000 basis points, USDX is in DEWS Warning territory — the highest stress band of any stablecoin in this market cap range. The disconnect between institutional-grade backing and catastrophic peg failure suggests the problem isn't the reserves but the infrastructure: deployed on Flare and Ozean with minimal DEX liquidity and no published proof of reserves, USDX lacks the on-chain arbitrage mechanisms that keep better-distributed stablecoins at par. Hex Trust has 270+ institutional clients and offices across five countries, but the USDX experience demonstrates that custodial relationships don't automatically translate into stablecoin stability when the on-chain market-making layer is absent.

pusd-plume.title: Plume's Wrapped Dollar
pusd-plume.text: pUSD is 100% backed by USDC held in a Nucleus BoringVault with zero-fee minting and redemption, deployed on both Ethereum and Plume Chain with on-chain custody and OFAC compliance checks — pragmatic if unambitious infrastructure for Plume's RWAfi ecosystem.
