The C- safety grade at 50 with a peg score of 72 and DEWS Watch band at 35 suggest the wrapper adds more friction than expected: 23 depeg events and thin DEX liquidity at $1.5 million TVL mean the secondary market doesn't always track the underlying USDC at par. USD1 and AUSD also approved as collateral adds optionality, though the current reserve is straightforwardly USDC. pUSD exists to give Plume a canonical stablecoin without building reserve infrastructure from scratch — the question is whether the wrapper adds enough value to justify the additional smart contract and custody risk over simply using USDC directly.

bold-liquity.title: Decentralization, Immutable
bold-liquity.text: Liquity V2's BOLD earns the highest safety grade of any DeFi stablecoin on the dashboard — an A at 84 — with perfect scores in both peg stability and decentralization, the only stablecoin to hit A+ 100 in both dimensions simultaneously. The reserve is 50% wstETH, 30% WETH, and 20% rETH in immutable contracts with no governance keys, no admin functions, and no RWA exposure — immutable-code governance that means any bug discovered post-deployment requires a full redeployment. The 90-rated redemption backstop with permissionless atomic collateral redemption at 50 basis points provides a structural peg floor, while user-set interest rates and yield amplification mechanics create self-correcting incentives that keep BOLD near par. Deployed across seven chains with only six depeg events on record, BOLD proves that genuine decentralization and peg stability are not competing objectives — though the modest market cap suggests the market still prefers convenience over ideological purity.

avusd-avant.title: Avalanche's Quiet Contender
avusd-avant.text: Avant's avUSD is 95% backed by USDC deployed into delta-neutral strategies via 0xPartners, with a 5% loss-absorption reserve — structurally a USDC wrapper that earns yield through the savUSD vault while maintaining 1:1 redeemability at a 5-basis-point fee. The institutional-unregulated custody and BVI domicile mean the trust assumptions run through Avant's operational integrity rather than a regulatory framework, which is why the backstop scores a modest 68 with queue-based redemptions that can take one to seven days. Five depeg events including one that hit 321 basis points below peg suggest the peg mechanism isn't bulletproof under stress, though the peg score of 99 indicates these were brief anomalies. In the Avalanche ecosystem, being the default stable-value token with yield attached is a defensible position — the question is whether unregulated custody and a BVI entity are the right foundations for the scale Avant is targeting.

ylds-figure.title: The SEC-Registered Yield Coin
ylds-figure.text: YLDS is that rarest of crypto products: a yield-bearing stablecoin registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and the Investment Company Act of 1940, paying SOFR minus 50 basis points through a fixed face-amount certificate structure that the SEC has explicitly blessed. The reserves are 86% overnight Treasury repos and 13% money market funds at UMB Bank, KPMG-audited, with institutional-top custody — a reserve stack so conservative it makes Circle look adventurous. Deployed on Solana and Provenance rather than Ethereum, YLDS targets a distribution path through Figure's existing lending platform rather than DeFi composability. The trade-off is clear: full SEC registration means mandatory KYC, restricted transferability, and zero DeFi integration, but for institutions that need a yield product whose legal status doesn't require a creative memo from outside counsel, YLDS is the only game in town.

usdq-quantoz.title: The Dutch Compliance Standard
usdq-quantoz.text: Quantoz's USDQ holds the distinction of being supervised by De Nederlandsche Bank under MiCAR with reserves maintained at 102% overcollateralization — 69% in Netherlands, German, and U.S. government bonds with 31% in cash at Tier 1 European banks, all held in segregated bankruptcy-remote accounts. A perfect peg score of 100 with zero depeg events and zero redemption fees makes USDQ the cleanest-performing USD stablecoin outside the top ten by every stability metric Pharos tracks. Deployed across Ethereum, Polygon, XRPL, and Algorand, the distribution is modest but the regulatory positioning is unmatched: DNB supervision, MiCAR compliance, and a Visa principal membership for stablecoin-linked debit cards turn compliance into competitive advantage. Whether the Dutch compliance premium translates into adoption at scale depends on whether European crypto users value regulatory certainty enough to choose USDQ over the familiar convenience of USDC.

usdn-noble.title: The Interchain Dollar
usdn-noble.text: Noble's USDN is backed 100% by short-term U.S. Treasury bills held in bankruptcy-remote SPVs via M0 Protocol, with a perfect peg score and only one depeg event followed by a 291-day streak at peg — the kind of stability record that makes the C+ safety grade look harsh until you see the F in decentralization and the absence of any DEX liquidity. As a rebasing yield-bearing stablecoin, USDN passes T-bill returns directly to holders, validators, and supporting platforms through M0's on-chain attestation framework, creating incentive alignment that most stablecoins ignore entirely. Noble has already facilitated billions in stablecoin transfers across Cosmos via IBC, so the distribution infrastructure is proven — the question is whether IBC-native reach can compete beyond the Cosmos ecosystem. The institutional-regulated custody and US jurisdiction provide a credible foundation, but the dependency on M0's infrastructure chain adds a layer of trust that the pristine T-bill backing was supposed to eliminate.

usdu-unitas.title: The JLP Hedge Fund
usdu-unitas.text: Unitas routes 80% of USDC deposits into Jupiter LP tokens — a basket of BTC, ETH, SOL, and USDC earning Jupiter Perps trading fees — while hedging the spot exposure with CEX perpetual shorts through Copper and Ceffu off-exchange settlement. The remaining 20% sits as margin for the short positions, making the entire reserve an active trading strategy with exotic collateral quality classification and zero idle assets. Singapore-domiciled with Accountable providing real-time zero-knowledge solvency proofs, USDu's transparency is a genuine upgrade over the 'trust us' school of yield products. Deployed on BSC and Solana with a peg score of 99 and only six depeg events, the machinery works — but the 80% dependency on USDC means every dollar of backing passes through Circle before reaching Jupiter's perps market, adding a layer of counterparty risk the hedge fund framing might obscure.

mnee-mnee.title: BSV's Dollar Envoy
mnee-mnee.text: MNEE is a fiat-backed stablecoin with 85% in sub-90-day T-bills and 15% in cash at a qualified custodian, attested by Wolf and Company P.C. — a clean reserve composition that earns an A+ in dependency risk and a peg score of 97. Originally launched on BSV before expanding to ERC-20, the migration suggests the team recognized that ecosystem size matters more than block size ideology, though Ethereum-only deployment with zero DEX liquidity limits on-chain exit routes. The C+ safety grade and B- in resilience reflect the institutional-unregulated custody and Antigua FSRC licensing that sit several tiers below the SEC or MAS in the global credibility hierarchy. The 16 depeg events including one that hit 601 basis points reveal the volatility of thin markets, but the peg has been stable enough that the C+ grade is more about infrastructure gaps than reserve quality.

usdg-paxos.title: Paxos's Singapore Sequel
usdg-paxos.text: After Binance's BUSD died under regulatory fire, Paxos relocated its stablecoin ambitions to Singapore, where USDG now sits under a MAS Major Payment Institution license with reserves split between DBS Bank and Standard Chartered — institutional-top custody that matches Circle and exceeds Tether. The all-very-low-risk reserve composition and A+ resilience grade make USDG structurally one of the safest stablecoins in existence, which makes the lowest peg score among rated top-ten coins a curious anomaly — a brief tracking history with early growing pains rather than structural fragility. The zero-fee redemption and additional EU issuance via a MiCA-compliant Finnish entity give USDG a dual-jurisdiction strategy that no competitor currently matches. The catch is on-chain presence: concentrated on just a few chains with modest DEX depth, USDG's institutional pedigree still outpaces its DeFi footprint.

xsgd-straitsx.title: Singapore's DeFi On-Ramp
xsgd-straitsx.text: XSGD is one of the few non-USD stablecoins with genuine regulatory credentials — 100% backed by SGD at DBS and Standard Chartered under a MAS Major Payment Institution license, with independent attestation reports issued twice monthly to ISCA standards. Deployed across five chains with institutional-regulated custody, XSGD has processed billions in combined on-chain volume with its USD sibling XUSD and expanded into real-world payment corridors through the Grab partnership and OKX Pay integration. The value proposition is specific: SGD-denominated on-chain liquidity for Southeast Asian payment flows where converting through USD pairs adds unnecessary FX friction. A rare case of a non-dollar stablecoin that serves a genuine economic function rather than existing as a novelty or regulatory experiment.

xusd-straitsx.title: Singapore's Dollar Export
xusd-straitsx.text: StraitsX's XUSD shares the same MAS Major Payment Institution framework as its XSGD sibling, with reserves split evenly between cash at DBS, Standard Chartered, and UOB, and short-term government securities — institutional-top custody earning A+ in both resilience and dependency risk. The C+ safety grade at 60 is entirely a liquidity story: an F at 22 with roughly $200K in DEX TVL that has collapsed over 99% in the past week, suggesting the on-chain market for XUSD is evaporating even as the institutional backing remains intact. The 123 depeg events and DEWS Watch band reflect this thin-market fragility rather than reserve inadequacy, a pattern familiar to well-backed stablecoins that never achieved DeFi critical mass. The real differentiator isn't the backing but the regional focus on SGD-USD forex flows for Southeast Asian payment corridors — a use case that doesn't need DEX liquidity to matter.

vgbp-vnx.title: Sterling on the Blockchain
vgbp-vnx.text: VNX's VGBP is backed 100% by GBP deposits at Swiss and Liechtenstein banks, AREVA audited (most recently December 2024) under Liechtenstein's FMA TVTG/Blockchain Act — one of vanishingly few GBP-pegged stablecoins on the market. The fourth most-traded fiat currency in the world has surprisingly little on-chain representation, giving VGBP an open field with almost no competition beyond BCP Technologies' FCA-registered tGBP. Deployed on Base and Celo with institutional-regulated custody, VGBP's two-chain distribution is narrower than its CHF and EUR siblings from VNX, reflecting the even thinner demand for on-chain sterling. Whether the UK's forthcoming stablecoin regulatory framework creates tailwinds for existing GBP tokens or invites banks to launch their own remains the existential question for the niche.

cusd-cap.title: The Stablecoin Basket Case
cusd-cap.text: Cap's cUSD is a basket wrapper backed by 35% USDC, 25% USDT, 20% BlackRock's BUIDL, 10% Franklin Templeton's BENJI, and 10% PayPal's PYUSD — five institutional-grade stablecoins blended into a single token with a maximum 40% concentration cap per asset. The dynamic-fee vault mechanism adjusts minting and redemption costs in real-time to prevent full utilization, ensuring atomic redemptions remain available, while EigenLayer AVS provides the economic security layer. Redemptions return a proportional basket of all underlying assets rather than a single stablecoin, which socializes any individual reserve depeg across all redeemers — clever risk distribution if everything works, shared contagion if one component fails. Ethereum-only deployment and wrapper-classified governance mean cUSD is less an independent stablecoin and more a diversification instrument for holders who want institutional RWA exposure without choosing sides.

msusd-main-street.title: Volatility Arbitrage in a Wrapper
msusd-main-street.text: Main Street USD is 100% backed by USDC with yield generated by deploying reserves into delta-neutral options volatility arbitrage strategies on centralized exchanges — a wrapper classified with CEX custody and exotic collateral quality. The C- safety grade at 52 with an F in resilience at 38 captures the concentration risk: the entire backing runs through CEX options infrastructure, and the broad owner upgrade authority on the proxy contract means the trust assumptions are decidedly retail-grade despite the institutional strategy framing. The 92-rated backstop is the bright spot — permissionless 1:1 USDC redemption provides a structural floor that most CEX-custodied stablecoins can't match. Whether ML-driven volatility arbitrage can consistently beat T-bill rates after fees is the central question — the claimed APY would be extraordinary in tradfi, which should calibrate your skepticism accordingly.

iusd-infinifi.title: Private Credit, Public Interface
iusd-infinifi.text: InfiniFi's iUSD is an on-chain credit fund wearing a stablecoin's clothing: 80% of reserves deployed into institutional private credit — Fasanara Capital, FalconX prime brokerage, Sentora's PYUSD strategy, Maple institutional lending — with the remaining 20% in liquid DeFi positions on Spark, Fluid, and Aave to service redemptions. The perfect peg score and zero depeg events mask the structural liquidity risk: when withdrawals spike, the queue-based redemption mechanism with 30-day processing windows means your exit depends on the credit book unwinding, not a swap. The DEWS Alert band — one of the highest stress readings on the dashboard — reflects exactly this tension, as heavy redemption pressure tests whether a fractional liquid reserve can absorb concentrated outflows. The exotic collateral quality classification is earned: private credit yields are real because the illiquidity risk is real, and the adequacy of a liquid buffer against an illiquid book is ultimately a function of how many holders test it simultaneously.

pht-pht.title: Peso Stablecoin Pioneer
pht-pht.text: PHT is a Philippine peso-pegged stablecoin built on a MakerDAO MCD fork, backed 100% by apcxUSDT (a 1:1 custodial USDT wrapper) in CDP vaults with Chainlink oracle price feeds — Singapore-domiciled with institutional-regulated custody. The reserve is technically high-risk not because USDT is unstable but because the apcxUSDT wrapper adds a custodial layer between PHT holders and the underlying Tether. Targeting the $38 billion Filipino remittance corridor where traditional fees eat 6%+ of every transfer, the use case is compelling but adoption requires merchant integration and fiat off-ramps that raw DeFi infrastructure doesn't provide. Ethereum-only deployment and the MCD fork architecture are battle-tested, but PHT remains a worthy experiment proving that local-currency stablecoins for emerging markets need distribution more than they need innovation.

hyusd-hylo.title: Solana's Native Stable
hyusd-hylo.text: Hylo's hyUSD is backed 90% by JitoSOL with the remaining 10% in other Solana LSTs — a concentration in a single liquid staking token that earns both an A+ in dependency risk (no upstream stablecoins) and a C+ in resilience (all-high-risk collateral on a mature alt-L1). The B- safety grade at 66 with a perfect peg score and only three depeg events is impressive for a stablecoin whose entire backing is volatile crypto derivatives, powered by a dual-token design where xSOL absorbs SOL price swings to maintain hyUSD's overcollateralization. Solana-only deployment with DAO governance earns a C+ in decentralization — a notable achievement among crypto-backed stablecoins, where most competitors rely on centralized admin controls. The oracle-free design is elegant in theory, but the 90% JitoSOL concentration means hyUSD's stability is a direct function of Jito's validator operations and the Solana staking ecosystem's health.

meusd-mezo.title: Bitcoin's Debt Position
meusd-mezo.text: Mezo's meUSD is what happens when Bitcoin maximalists discover CDPs — backed 100% by BTC in various wrapped forms (tBTC, WBTC, SolvBTC, cbBTC) with a minimum 110% collateral ratio and Liquity-style redemption mechanics. The D safety grade at 49 with an F in decentralization reflects the unproven chain penalty from Mezo's Bitcoin L2, which drags the entire score despite a B+ in resilience and an 87-rated backstop with permissionless collateral redemption. The 184 depeg events and a peg score of 80 with only 72% time at peg show the volatility cost of BTC-only collateral at aggressive collateral ratios — when Bitcoin moves, meUSD moves with it until arbitrageurs close the gap. DEWS in the Watch band and two-chain deployment across Ethereum and Mezo L2 capture the current state: a principled Bitcoin-native CDP that has found a niche audience but not stability at scale.

usdu-usdu-finance.title: The Adapter Stablecoin
usdu-usdu-finance.text: USDU Finance takes a modular approach where tokens can only be minted through DAO-approved adapters connected to Curve (35%), TermMax fixed-rate vaults (35%), and Morpho (30%) — all held as adapter-owned LP tokens and vault shares, not user balances. The danger notice on the dashboard says it plainly: USDU is intentionally undercollateralized at roughly 43%, designed for professional market participants who understand the risk. The DEWS Alert band at 40 with 94% pool stress and a DEX price spread of over 500 basis points confirm this isn't a product optimized for retail safety. The Curve adapter dynamically manages liquidity based on pool imbalance while TermMax enables fixed-rate lending for RWA collateral — sophisticated engineering for a $5 million product that explicitly prioritizes capital efficiency over the overcollateralization most stablecoins consider table stakes.

uty-xsy.title: Avalanche's Ethena
uty-xsy.text: XSY's Unity applies the delta-neutral playbook to AVAX — 30% USDC deposits converted into 35% long AVAX spot and 35% short AVAX perpetual futures, custodied at Ceffu and Copper Clearloop. The F safety grade at 37 pairs a near-perfect peg score with an F in resilience at 16 — the predictable consequence of CEX custody, exotic collateral quality, and zero DEX liquidity on a single chain classified as an established alt-L1. The DEWS score of literally zero is the lowest stress reading on the entire Pharos dashboard, suggesting the product is operationally dormant rather than operationally risky. Whether the AVAX perpetual futures market has sufficient depth and consistent positive funding to sustain this model remains the central question, but the 7-day unbonding period for redemptions and absent DEX presence suggest UTY is currently more infrastructure than product.

gusd-gate.title: Exchange Scrip, RWA Edition
gusd-gate.text: Gate's GUSD is a yield-bearing stablecoin that functions more like an investment certificate than a medium of exchange — users stake USDT or USDC on Gate and receive GUSD whose value accrues interest, payable at redemption. The reserve is 70% short-term T-bills with 25% in stablecoin deposits and 5% in yield strategies, but the CEX custody and self-reported proof of reserves with a promise to 'gradually disclose' details earn it a D in resilience and an F in decentralization. Deployed on Ethereum but with zero DEX liquidity, GUSD exists entirely within Gate's walled garden — a product whose utility begins and ends at the exchange's own interface. The C- safety grade accurately captures a stablecoin that is structurally sound but operationally opaque, useful within its ecosystem and essentially invisible outside it.

usdcv-societe-generale-forge.title: A Bank's Stablecoin
usdcv-societe-generale-forge.text: SG-FORGE's USDCV is the first USD stablecoin issued by a major European bank — 100% backed by cash at BNY Mellon in segregated bankruptcy-remote accounts, earning institutional-top custody and A+ in both resilience and dependency risk with a DEWS score of 1 — the calmest stablecoin on the entire dashboard. Only two depeg events in its history and a 163-day peg streak demonstrate the stability you'd expect when a systemically important bank with a trillion euros in assets underwrites the reserve. The C+ safety grade at 62 is entirely a liquidity and decentralization story: F-rated in both, with just $2.3 million in DEX TVL from a single pool, and US persons explicitly excluded from participation. USDCV is arguably the most over-regulated stablecoin in existence — MiCA-compliant EMI license, daily reserve disclosure, BNY custody — waiting for the on-chain liquidity to match its institutional pedigree.

usdai-usd-ai.title: GPU Yield in Dollar Clothing
usdai-usd-ai.text: Peel back the AI branding and USD.AI is a stablecoin backed 56% by M0's T-bill tokens and 43% by PayPal's PYUSD — a surprisingly conventional reserve for a product that markets itself at the intersection of artificial intelligence and finance. The 1% allocated to GPU-collateralized loans — NVIDIA hardware tokenized as warehouse receipts under UCC law — is what makes it interesting, but that's also the only part that justifies the name. The 218 depeg events and a worst deviation of nearly 1500 basis points tell a rougher story than the current peg suggests, and the 30-day redemption windows through a QEV auction mechanism mean exiting USDai is a patience exercise, not a swap. The C- safety grade reflects the accumulated dependency chain: USDai depends on M0, which depends on T-bills in unregulated custody, and on PYUSD, which depends on Paxos — three layers of counterparty risk between a holder and a government bond.

usx-solstice.title: The Solana Wrapper
usx-solstice.text: Solstice's USX is structurally simpler than its Swiss pedigree and Galaxy Digital backing might suggest: 55% USDC and 45% USDT, minted 1:1, with Chainlink Proof of Reserve verifying the reserves on-chain. Classified as a wrapper with governance quality reflecting its pass-through nature, USX inherits the safety profile of its underlying stablecoins rather than creating its own — which makes the value proposition a question of Solana-native convenience rather than novel design. The KYC-gated institutional minting at a $500K minimum coexists with permissionless DEX access, creating a two-tier system where large minters get direct access and everyone else trades the secondary market. Plans to expand collateral to SOL, ETH, and BTC would change the risk profile entirely, but for now USX is a regulated stablecoin wrapper on a chain that already has USDC and USDT.

hollar-hydrated.title: Polkadot's Home Dollar
hollar-hydrated.text: HOLLAR is Hydration's overcollateralized stablecoin — 40% DOT, 15% ETH, 15% vDOT (liquid staked), 10% WBTC/tBTC, 15% USDT/USDC, and 5% giga-tokens — built on Aave V3-forked code on Polkadot's largest DeFi protocol. The C- safety grade at 50 with an F in decentralization at zero reflects the unproven chain penalty from the Hydration appchain, while the 83-rated backstop and B+ resilience from the Stability Module's automated partial liquidations provide structural soundness. A peg score of 96 with only seven depeg events and DEWS Calm at 9 show controlled stability on a small scale — Hydration is clearly prioritizing controlled growth over aggressive expansion. Whether a Polkadot-native stablecoin can attract users beyond the DOT ecosystem's existing DeFi participants remains the existential question for a chain tier that Pharos classifies as unproven.

musd-metamask.title: The Wallet Becomes the Bank
musd-metamask.text: MetaMask's mUSD is what happens when the world's most popular self-custodial wallet decides 30 million monthly users should have their own stablecoin — issued by Stripe's Bridge using M0 protocol infrastructure, with 85% in T-bills and 15% in cash held in bankruptcy-remote custody with real-time on-chain validator attestations. The C+ safety grade at 64 pairs a near-perfect peg score with B+ resilience and a DEWS reading of just 5 — the least stressed stablecoin in this batch — while supply has grown over 27% in a single month, signaling early adoption momentum. The F in decentralization is the cost of centralized issuance through Bridge, but the distribution advantage is structural: mUSD is native to the wallet where most DeFi users already live, making every new MetaMask user a potential mUSD holder without an additional onboarding step. Deployed on Ethereum and Linea, plans for yield sharing and MetaMask Card spending at Mastercard merchants signal ambitions well beyond DeFi — the wallet becoming the bank.

cash-phantom.title: The Wallet's Dollar
cash-phantom.text: Phantom wallet's CASH is what happens when crypto's most popular Solana wallet decides its users should have a native stablecoin — issued through Stripe's Bridge infrastructure with reserves in T-bills, reverse repos, money market funds, and bank deposits, all held in segregated bankruptcy-remote accounts under FinCEN and state money transmitter licenses. The C+ safety grade with a near-perfect peg score and B+ resilience reflects genuinely conservative backing: 90% of reserves in very-low-risk assets with tokenized treasuries from BUIDL and USTB rounding out the portfolio. Solana-only deployment keeps it focused on Phantom's home turf, where distribution through the wallet's existing user base provides an on-ramp advantage no DeFi protocol can match. The F in decentralization is the cost of centralized issuance through BBI, but for Phantom's user base, the trade-off between decentralization purity and in-wallet convenience was never close.

tgbp-tokenised.title: Sterling's Lone Ranger
tgbp-tokenised.text: BCP Technologies' tGBP is backed 100% by GBP cash and UK gilts (zero-coupon, segregated) with Enumis custody, holding the distinction of being the UK's first FCA-registered GBP stablecoin (FRN 928840) having graduated from the regulatory sandbox. Deployed across five chains including Ethereum, Base, BSC, Polygon, and Avalanche with institutional-regulated custody, tGBP has broader distribution than its modest market cap suggests. The Wirex integration brought it to millions of potential users, but GBP stablecoins collectively remain a rounding error in a dollar-dominated market. Its real significance lies in being the regulatory template that every subsequent UK stablecoin issuer will be measured against — the first FCA registration is a precedent that carries weight regardless of the token's current scale.

eurau-allunity.title: Deutsche Boerse's Euro Bet
eurau-allunity.text: AllUnity's EURAU is backed 100% by euro deposits at CRR-eligible EU credit institutions, BaFin-licensed as an EMI under MiCA, with institutional-regulated custody and integration into Deutsche Boerse's Clearstream infrastructure — more institutional credibility than most euro stablecoins combined. Backed by DWS (Deutsche Bank's asset management arm), Galaxy Digital, and Flow Traders, the sponsor list reads like a TradFi-crypto bridge roster. Deployed across five EVM chains (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon), EURAU has broader L2 reach than competing euro stablecoins that remain Ethereum-only. The problem is the denominator: euro stablecoins represent a fraction of the global stablecoin market, making EURAU simultaneously one of the best-backed euro tokens and a reminder of how thoroughly the dollar dominates this space.

usdh-native-markets.title: Hyperliquid's Chosen One
usdh-native-markets.text: Native Markets beat Paxos, Ethena, and Frax in a validator vote to become Hyperliquid's native stablecoin issuer, and the reserve composition justifies the confidence: 40% short-term T-bills managed by BlackRock at JP Morgan, 20% tokenized treasuries via BUIDL and USTB, 20% cash at JP Morgan and Lead Bank, with the rest in repos and treasury funds. Issued through Bridge Building Inc. — Stripe's stablecoin subsidiary — with BPM LLP attestations and FinCEN MSB registration, USDH brings institutional-regulated custody to a chain where most dollars previously flowed through Circle. The C+ safety grade at 61 reflects the single-chain HyperEVM deployment and 48 liquidity score, but the A+ resilience and near-perfect peg score suggest the product is stronger than its ecosystem concentration implies. The real play is capturing the yield from Hyperliquid's USDC deposits that currently flows to Circle — a revenue redirection that validators explicitly chose.

sbc-brale.title: The Plumber's Stablecoin
sbc-brale.text: Brale's SBC is backed 50% by cash and 50% by short-duration T-bills with Abdo attestations, deployed across ten chains — the broadest distribution of any stablecoin under $20 million in market cap. The C+ safety grade at 64 with a peg score of 96 and D in decentralization reflects the trade-offs of a US-licensed money transmitter (FinCEN MSB) operating a reference implementation rather than a competitive product. Built by Dwolla's founder, SBC optimizes for boring reliability: institutional-regulated custody, consistent peg, and the broadest possible chain coverage to demonstrate Brale's stablecoin-as-a-service platform capabilities. The real product is Brale itself — the infrastructure layer that lets other companies issue their own compliant stablecoins; SBC is the reference implementation, and the clients are the business.

euri-banking-circle.title: Binance's Euro
euri-banking-circle.text: Eurite is the euro stablecoin endorsed by Binance, issued by Banking Circle S.A. under a Luxembourg CSSF credit institution license with MiCA compliance — 70% euro cash in segregated fiduciary accounts and 30% in EU government securities, attested by Ernst & Young. The C+ safety grade at 61 pairs an A+ peg score of 98 with an F-adjacent liquidity score of 32, reflecting the gap between institutional backing and thin on-chain trading depth that plagues most euro stablecoins. Binance's distribution muscle gives EURI instant access to the world's largest exchange, but the DEWS Watch band and 38 depeg events suggest the secondary market hasn't yet achieved the depth that exchange endorsement was supposed to provide. Whether the Binance imprimatur can make a euro stablecoin stick where Circle's EURC and SocGen's EURCV are also competing remains the central question for the entire euro stablecoin market.

msusd-metronome.title: Synths Still Standing
msusd-metronome.text: Metronome's msUSD is a synthetic dollar from the pre-yield-farming era that somehow kept its users — minted against 30% USDC, 25% Vesper yield tokens, 20% DAI, and 20% ETH/WBTC/sfrxETH, with no direct redemption mechanism, only debt repayment. The C+ safety grade at 62 with balanced B+ scores across peg stability, liquidity, and resilience is remarkably consistent for a product this niche, though the B- in dependency risk reflects exposure to DAI, USDC, and the legacy FRAX in its collateral basket. Supply has spiked over 40% in a single week — an unusual surge for a synthetic asset that most of DeFi has forgotten about, suggesting renewed interest or a single large minter. The zero-slippage intra-protocol synth swaps remain a neat trick in a market where synthetic assets have largely fallen out of fashion, and the 63-day peg streak shows the collateral-provider buyback mechanism is doing its job.

aznd-mu-digital.title: Asia Credit Goes On-Chain
aznd-mu-digital.text: Mu Digital's AZND tokenizes Asian credit instruments — 30% sovereign bonds (BBB+ min), 35% investment-grade corporate and bank bonds, 15% high-yield industrial bonds, and 20% private credit — managed by Singapore-regulated Golden Hill Asset Management with muBOND junior tranche providing ~118% overcollateralization. The C- safety grade at 50 with an F in liquidity and a D in resilience reflects institutional-unregulated custody on Monad (an unproven chain) with all four reserve categories rated high risk despite their investment-grade classification in traditional markets. As a NAV-appreciating token with weekly redemptions via KYC-gated USDC minting and Accountable real-time proof of reserves, AZND targets a market historically reserved for institutional desks and private banks. Whether DeFi users accustomed to double-digit yields will find single-digit returns from Asian corporates compelling enough to bridge the trust gap remains the central question.

nect-beraborrow.title: Berachain's Liquity Fork
nect-beraborrow.text: BeraBorrow's NECT is a Liquity-style CDP on Berachain accepting the chain's native menagerie — 40% iBGT, 25% iBERA/WBERA, plus wrapped BTC variants, ETH derivatives, and Kodiak LP tokens — all classified as high-risk exotic collateral on an unproven chain, which is why the safety grade reads F at 36 with a zero in decentralization. An active depeg since mid-March and DEWS in the Alert band at 41 confirm the stress: with a market cap under $600K and just $43K in DEX liquidity, NECT is too small to attract the arbitrageurs needed to close the peg gap. The 84-rated backstop from the Liquity-style collateral redemption mechanism provides a structural floor, and the auto-compounding dens that reinvest rewards into collateral are a clever twist on the CDP model. Whether NECT becomes Berachain's canonical dollar depends entirely on whether Berachain itself achieves escape velocity — at current scale, it's a well-designed product waiting for an ecosystem to grow around it.

usp-pikudao.title: Turkish Carry Trade, Tokenized
usp-pikudao.text: PikuDAO's USP is a NAV-appreciating token — 50% deployed into a Turkish lira FX arbitrage strategy via Balsa Technologies (delta-neutral TRY/USD trades capturing Turkey's inflation-driven carry), 40% across DeFi protocols (Giza, Almanak, USD.AI, Ethena, Aave, Cap), and 10% in a USDC/USDT buffer. The very-high risk classification on the Turkish FX strategy and high risk on the DeFi allocations are reflected in the exotic collateral quality rating and a backstop of 65 with whitelisted queue-based redemptions at 0.2% fee — KYC/KYB required to mint or redeem, with a 24-hour FIFO settlement queue. It's a genuinely novel yield source for DeFi — Turkish carry trade returns are uncorrelated with crypto markets — but also one that concentrates geopolitical and counterparty risk in a single emerging market whose currency has lost over 90% against the dollar in a decade. The NAV has appreciated above $1.07, which proves the strategy works when it works — the question is what happens when it doesn't.

pmusd-precious-metals.title: Gold-Backed With Extra Steps
pmusd-precious-metals.text: RAAC's pmUSD routes tokenized gold from I-ON Digital through overcollateralized CDPs to produce a dollar-pegged stablecoin — 100% backed by ION.au with real-time Chainlink Proof of Reserves and Instruxi attestations verifying the gold holdings. The 348 depeg events and a peg score of 73 reveal what happens when your collateral trades in a different currency than your peg: gold price movements create constant drift that the CDP mechanism must continuously absorb. Deployed only on Ethereum with institutional-unregulated custody and DEWS in the Watch band, pmUSD's persistent below-peg trading reflects the structural challenge of maintaining a dollar peg against a commodity collateral base. The transparency is genuine — real-time on-chain verification of gold reserves is more than most RWA-backed stablecoins offer — but transparency about the mechanism doesn't eliminate the mechanism's inherent friction.

jupusd-jupiter.title: Jupiter's BlackRock Dollar
jupusd-jupiter.text: JupUSD is Jupiter's bid to own the dollar layer on Solana — 90% backed by Ethena's USDtb (which itself holds BlackRock's BUIDL fund shares) with a 10% USDC buffer, custodied by Porto/Anchorage Digital under a GENIUS-compliant framework. A peg score of 99 and a DEWS reading of just 1 — the lowest stress score in this batch — reflect a product that has launched cleanly, though the absence of tracked DEX liquidity suggests JupUSD circulates primarily within Jupiter's own ecosystem rather than the broader Solana DeFi market. The plan to convert JLP's USDC holdings into JupUSD is as much a revenue play as a product launch: every dollar moved from USDC to JupUSD redirects reserve yield from Circle to Jupiter's ecosystem. The dependency chain runs JupUSD → USDtb → BUIDL → actual Treasuries — three layers between holder and government bonds, each adding operational risk while the underlying asset remains pristine.

u-united-stables.title: The Stablecoin of Stablecoins
u-united-stables.text: United Stables' U is exactly what it sounds like: a dollar backed by other dollars — 35% USDC, 35% USDT, 15% World Liberty Financial's USD1, and 15% fiat and T-bills, minted 1:1 by depositing any of the whitelisted stablecoins. The A in dependency risk and 89-rated backstop reflect the strength of the underlying assets; the C- in resilience and F in decentralization reflect the wrapper itself — a BVI entity with unregulated Bermuda custody adding a layer of counterparty risk on top of stablecoins that already carry their own. At over a billion dollars in circulation with zero depeg events, U has functioned as designed, though the DEWS Watch band suggests the market sees stress signals that the peg hasn't yet absorbed. The honest question is why a holder would accept the additional custody and smart contract risk of wrapping USDC and USDT when they could simply hold the originals.

reusd-re-protocol.title: Reinsurance Meets DeFi
reusd-re-protocol.text: Re Protocol's reUSD channels deposits into reinsurance contracts and delta-neutral ETH basis trades — 50% in sUSDe/USDe positions, 30% in short-duration T-bills, and 20% in USDC as a redemption buffer. The C+ safety grade and peg score of 53 reflect the exotic collateral quality and the dependency on Ethena's infrastructure, while the NAV-appreciating price above $1 means reUSD is measuring yield accrual, not peg stability. The queue-based redemption at 69 backstop score with 20% of supply as immediate capacity provides a structural floor, though the BVI FSC license and real-time Chainlink attestations via The Network Firm add layers of verification that most yield products skip. The target of risk-free-rate-plus-250-basis-points sounds pedestrian until you consider the yield sources are genuinely uncorrelated with DeFi lending markets — reinsurance premiums don't care about on-chain utilization rates.

rwausdi-multipli.title: The RWA Middleware Layer
rwausdi-multipli.text: Multipli's rwaUSDi wraps 100+ tokenized treasury products, gold tokens, and market-neutral fund units into a single mintable stablecoin — 50% in tokenized T-bills (BUIDL, USDY, OUSG), 25% in aggregated treasury-backed stablecoins, 15% in tokenized gold, and 10% in institutional fund units from Nomura, Fasanara, and Edge Capital. The pitch is that lending protocols can't individually underwrite hundreds of RWA tokens, so rwaUSDi does the aggregation and due diligence — backed by a Lloyd's insurance policy covering de-pegging risk, which is a genuinely novel backstop for a stablecoin. UAE-domiciled with AFI-audited on-chain reserves, it operates on Ethereum only with KYB-gated institutional minting, making it less a retail product and more a composable RWA building block. The elegant abstraction adds a trust layer between holder and underlying assets, but with 99 peg score and only two depeg events on record, the machinery has functioned as designed.

pusd-pleasing.title: Hong Kong Gold, Arbitrum Rails
pusd-pleasing.text: Pleasing International's PUSD is 90% a USDT wrapper with 10% tokenized gold exposure through PGOLD — a hybrid that is neither a pure dollar peg nor a gold-backed token, and the market has noticed. Trading at a 645-basis-point discount to peg with an active depeg event running since December 2024 and DEWS in the Alert band, PUSD is one of the most stressed stablecoins on the dashboard. The Hong Kong-based precious metals firm's institutional-unregulated custody and Arbitrum-plus-ApeChain deployment offer no redemption backstop modeled by Pharos, meaning holders facing a 6.5% discount have no clear path to par value. PUSD serves as a real-time case study in what happens when a stablecoin's peg mechanism fails to attract the arbitrageurs needed to close the gap.

usdm-mega.title: Funding the Sequencer
usdm-mega.text: MegaETH's USDm flips the L2 business model: instead of extracting sequencer fees from users, it uses reserve yield from Ethena's USDtb (90% of backing, itself holding BlackRock's BUIDL) to subsidize network operations — the chain literally gets cheaper as more people hold its native stablecoin. A perfect peg score and only two depeg events with DEWS at 2 suggest the product is functioning cleanly, though the absence of any tracked DEX liquidity means exit routes are limited to the redemption mechanism. The dependency on Ethena's infrastructure for both reserve management and custody adds counterparty risk that the underlying Treasury bills don't carry, and the stablecoin's value proposition is inseparable from MegaETH's own traction as an L2. The economics reveal a flywheel where stablecoin adoption subsidizes network costs which drives adoption — elegant when it works, but the flywheel spins in both directions.

usat-tether.title: Tether Comes Home
usat-tether.text: After years of operating from El Salvador, Tether launched a US-regulated stablecoin through Anchorage Digital Bank under the GENIUS Act — 80% T-bills and 20% cash, issued under an OCC federal bank charter with Cantor Fitzgerald as reserve custodian. A perfect peg score and zero depeg events on barely $28 million in circulation suggest USA-T is still in early deployment, while the DEWS Watch band and a liquidity score of 9 reflect the near-absence of secondary market trading. The dual-product strategy — USA-T for US compliance, USDT for global liquidity — is Tether's answer to Circle's home-turf advantage, backed by billions in annual revenue and the organizational capacity to scale rapidly once distribution channels open. Whether Tether can win the trust of US institutions that have spent years scrutinizing its offshore operations is the question USA-T was built to answer.

yzusd-yuzu.title: Yield Vault in Stable Clothing
yzusd-yuzu.text: Yuzu's yzUSD packages curated DeFi yield strategies into an overcollateralized stablecoin — 50% Pendle PT/LP positions, 20% Euler/Morpho lending, 20% other DeFi strategies, and a 10% USDT0 buffer — all classified as exotic collateral on an unproven chain (Plasma). A perfect peg score and zero depeg events sound reassuring until you note the absence of any DEX liquidity and queue-based redemptions scoring just 56 on the backstop, with the yzPP junior tranche absorbing first losses. The strict KYC gating — only accredited, qualified, or institutional investors can mint and redeem — makes yzUSD one of the most access-restricted stablecoins in DeFi, which explains both the zero depeg events (few holders means few sellers) and the non-existent secondary market. It's a yield aggregator that happens to maintain a dollar peg rather than a stablecoin that happens to generate yield — the distinction matters when things go wrong.

nusd-neutrl.title: OTC Discounts, Tokenized
nusd-neutrl.text: Neutrl's NUSD monetizes the gap between OTC-discounted locked tokens and their spot market value — 60% in delta-neutral basis trades, 20% in liquid stablecoins, and 20% in hedged OTC locked-token positions sourced via STIX at 30-70% discounts. At $200 million in circulation with only four depeg events and a peg score of 99, the strategy has scaled impressively, backed by Accountable's real-time proof of solvency and institutional custody through Fireblocks and Copper. The DEWS Watch band and recent supply contraction suggest the market is testing the exit door, which is a queue-based redemption at 70-rated backstop — not instant, but structured. The strategy's capacity is inherently limited by OTC deal flow, but the massive token unlock overhang across the crypto market provides years of raw material for a trade that hedge funds have run privately and NUSD has tokenized publicly.

usdgo-osl.title: Asia's On-Ramp Dollar
usdgo-osl.text: OSL Group's USDGO pairs a Hong Kong-listed company's distribution network with Anchorage Digital's OCC federal bank charter — 80% T-bills and 20% cash, earning a perfect peg score with zero depeg events and a C+ safety grade at 64 constrained only by the F in decentralization and absent DEX liquidity. The institutional-regulated custody and GENIUS Act compliance give it credentials that most Asia-focused stablecoins lack, targeting the e-commerce, gaming, and trade settlement corridor rather than DeFi composability. Deployed on Solana only, USDGO's distribution strategy follows OSL's institutional client relationships rather than the permissionless on-chain playbook. A narrower niche than general-purpose competitors, but potentially more defensible — the kind of stablecoin that succeeds through business development rather than token incentives.

fidd-fidelity.title: Fidelity's Trillion-Dollar Entrance
fidd-fidelity.text: When the third-largest asset manager on earth launches a stablecoin, the signal matters more than the product — and FIDD's product is textbook institutional: 80% T-bills and 20% cash at BNY Mellon, PwC-attested, OCC national trust charter, earning institutional-top custody and a B- safety grade at 67 with A+ in peg stability, resilience, and dependency risk. The perfect peg score and zero depeg events reflect what happens when Fidelity's compliance infrastructure backs a dollar token, though the D in liquidity at 43 reveals that institutional pedigree hasn't yet translated into DeFi depth. Supply is contracting — an early-stage product still finding its distribution channels across Fidelity Crypto, Fidelity Digital Assets, and the wealth advisory platform. Underestimating Fidelity's distribution muscle would be unwise, but the Ethereum-only deployment and declining circulation suggest the trillion-dollar entrance is still more signal than scale.

aid-gaib.title: GPU Yield, Dollarized
aid-gaib.text: GAIB's AID is a conventional dollar stablecoin — T-bills and stablecoin reserves, 1:1 mint and burn — whose entire reason for existing is its companion token sAID, which accrues yield from GPU and AI infrastructure financing deals. The structure neatly separates stable value (AID) from exotic yield (sAID), letting users choose their risk exposure. At $21 million market cap it's early-stage even by RWA standards, betting that AI compute demand will create a durable yield substrate. Whether GPU financing agreements produce reliable enough cash flows to back a yield product is genuinely untested — but in a market where every new stablecoin needs a narrative, "AI infrastructure yield" is at least more substantive than most.

apxusd-apyx.title: Dividends as Collateral
apxusd-apyx.text: Apyx introduced what might be the most creative collateral backing in stablecoins: preferred shares from Digital Asset Treasury companies — publicly traded equity from firms like Strategy that hold large crypto positions. The theory is that variable-rate preferred shares trade near par regardless of crypto price volatility, providing stable collateral for a dollar token. Launched on Ethereum in February 2026 with DeFi Development Corp as an early investor, apxUSD is so new that market cap data barely exists. The Protocol-Owned Liquidity buffer is meant to absorb stress, but the underlying question is whether equity dividends from crypto-holding companies are truly uncorrelated with the crypto market they depend on.

jpyc-jpyc.title: The Yen's Licensed Pioneer
jpyc-jpyc.text: Japan's first FSA-approved yen stablecoin occupies an enviable regulatory position — Type II Funds Transfer license under the Payment Services Act, 100% backed by JPY deposits and Japanese government bonds, with institutional-regulated custody and zero transaction fees. Deployed on three chains with the JPYC EX platform handling mint/redemption via bank transfer after KYC, the infrastructure is sound but the market cap remains modest — a product that proves regulatory compliance alone doesn't drive adoption. The real threat isn't GYEN (regulated in New York but locked out of Japan's domestic market) but Progmat Coin from Mitsubishi UFJ, Sumitomo Mitsui, and Mizuho — three megabanks whose combined balance sheet makes JPYC look like a rounding error. Being first to market matters less when the second movers have trillion-dollar balance sheets and existing banking relationships with every corporation in Japan.

xaut-tether.title: Tether Mints Bullion
xaut-tether.text: Tether's gold token is backed 100% by LBMA Good Delivery bars in Swiss vaults with BDO Italia attestations, operating under El Salvador's CNAD jurisdiction with institutional-regulated custody — the same transparency framework as USDT, applied to physical bullion. XAUT commands the largest share of the tokenized gold market, which sounds impressive until you notice that share has been eroding as PAXG and newer competitors chip away at the margins. Deployed on Ethereum only, XAUT works exactly like you'd expect from Tether: a market that trades on brand recognition over the granular bar-level transparency that Paxos offers with PAXG's allocated serial numbers. With gold's rally inflating all boats, XAUT's real significance may be Tether's own physical gold accumulation rather than the tokenized wrapper itself.

paxg-paxos.title: Fort Knox With a Charter
paxg-paxos.text: The only federally regulated gold token in existence, PAXG operates under Paxos's OCC national trust charter with institutional-top custody, KPMG monthly attestations, and individually allocated LBMA Good Delivery bars at Brink's London — each with a serial number verifiable on the Paxos platform. The permanent second to Tether Gold by market share, PAXG is the first choice for anyone whose compliance department has veto power: allocated bars, bankruptcy-remote trust structure, and the kind of regulatory paper trail that makes institutional allocators comfortable. While XAUT trades on Tether's brand recognition, PAXG trades on verifiable custody — in a market where gold itself is the product, trust infrastructure is the only real differentiator. Ethereum-only deployment limits DeFi composability but matches the product's institutional focus.

kau-kinesis.title: Gold That Pays Rent
kau-kinesis.text: Kinesis cracked the code that other gold tokens missed: people want yield. KAU holders earn a share of 15% of all platform transaction fees, paid monthly in additional gold — backed 1:1 by LBMA-approved physical gold at 1 gram per token in ABX vaults, Bureau Veritas audited, under a Cayman CIMA VASP license. Add a virtual Mastercard for point-of-sale gold spending and you get something genuinely different: gold that functions as money, not just an asset, with institutional-regulated custody and independent attestation that the bars actually exist. The catch is that yield depends entirely on Kinesis's transaction volume — if trading dries up, so does the rent check, and without any tracked on-chain contracts, KAU exists primarily within Kinesis's own platform rather than the broader DeFi ecosystem. A growing challenger to the XAUT-PAXG duopoly, betting that yield and spendability matter more than Ethereum composability.

xaum-matrixdock.title: Asia's Institutional Bullion
xaum-matrixdock.text: Matrixdock's XAUm is backed by LBMA-certified 99.99% gold bars at Brink's and Malca-Amit in Singapore and Hong Kong, Bureau Veritas audited, with institutional-regulated custody and a minimum redemption of 32.148 XAUm (1 kg) restricted to KYC'd accredited investors. The Asia-Pacific custody thesis — Singapore and Hong Kong vaults rather than London or Switzerland — is a deliberate choice targeting institutions that prefer regional domicile for their gold exposure. Deployed on Ethereum and BSC, XAUm remains a modest share of the tokenized gold market, but the partnership with Bhutan's Gelephu Mindfulness City for sovereign gold tokenization signals ambitions beyond retail. Whether institutions actually prefer Asia-domiciled custody over the London and Swiss vaults that XAUT and PAXG offer remains the strategic bet.

gold-vro.title: Gold in the Free Ports
gold-vro.text: VeraOne stores its gold in the Geneva Free Ports — the same duty-free Swiss storage complex favored by art collectors and sovereign wealth funds — which gives VRO perhaps the most interesting custody story in tokenized gold and absolutely none of the liquidity to match. At $48 million market cap with minimal trading volume, it's a micro-cap gold gram token that proves having premium vault infrastructure doesn't automatically attract premium capital. The 1 VRO = 1 gram denomination makes it accessible on paper, but without meaningful exchange listings or DeFi integrations, accessibility remains theoretical.

cgo-comtech.title: DMCC-Stamped Bullion
cgo-comtech.text: ComTech Gold's CGO is backed 1:1 by 24-karat 999.9% physical gold at 1 gram per token in Transguard vaults under the Emirates Group umbrella, DMCC endorsed, with individually serialized bars registered on DMCC Tradeflow and institutional-regulated custody under DAFZA jurisdiction. The redemption-via-app workflow with minimum 10-gram delivery is the most retail-friendly physical gold offramp in the tokenized gold market, leveraging Dubai's regulatory clarity on tokenized commodities that is genuinely ahead of most jurisdictions. Without tracked on-chain contracts, CGO exists primarily within the ComTech ecosystem rather than DeFi, and none of the UAE pedigree has translated into meaningful global adoption. Impeccable local credentials, negligible global presence — proving once again that regulatory clarity alone doesn't create liquidity.

dgld-gold-token-sa.title: Heritage Gold, Rebooted
dgld-gold-token-sa.text: DGLD is backed 1:1 by allocated LBMA Good Delivery PAMP gold bars — the Swiss refiner whose name is synonymous with premium bullion — at 1 troy ounce per token with real-time reserve verification through on-chain bar serial numbers and VQF/FINMA regulatory oversight. MKS PAMP relaunched DGLD in late 2025 with deployments on Ethereum and Base, institutional-regulated custody, and minimum 1-gram redemption — the lowest physical gold redemption threshold of any tokenized gold product. A 60-year refining heritage and the most prestigious gold backing in crypto have produced one of the least adopted gold tokens on the market, proving that heritage is necessary but wildly insufficient for winning the tokenized gold race. The dual-chain deployment signals ambition beyond the institutional market, but DGLD's traction remains a fraction of what PAMP's reputation would suggest.

kag-kinesis.title: The Lonely Ounce
kag-kinesis.text: KAG is backed 1:1 by investment-grade physical silver at 1 troy ounce per token, Bureau Veritas audited under a Cayman CIMA VASP license — the same yield-sharing model as its gold sibling KAU, where holders earn a share of 15% of all platform transaction fees paid monthly in additional silver. In a world where tokenized gold has surged past $6 billion, tokenized silver remains a ghost town and KAG is effectively its only resident. Deployed on Ethereum with institutional-regulated custody, the product is structurally identical to KAU but without the macro tailwind: silver's performance has lagged gold's rally dramatically, limiting both demand and yield generation. The thesis is straightforward — if precious metals tokenization is real, silver must eventually follow gold — but 'eventually' is doing a lot of heavy lifting for a product this niche.

eurq-quantoz.title: The Enterprise Euro
eurq-quantoz.text: Quantoz built EURQ for corporate treasurers, not DeFi degens — DNB-regulated under MiCA, 102% reserved in 68% eurozone government bonds and 32% cash at Tier 1 European banks, with direct SEPA integration and institutional-regulated custody. The same Dutch compliance infrastructure as its USDQ sibling, EURQ carves a niche in programmable corporate payments where compliance is a feature, not a tax. The 2% over-collateralization buffer and self-reported transparency are a quiet flex: enough to signal conservatism without dragging capital efficiency, supervised by the same DNB that oversees ING and ABN AMRO. Whether the enterprise market actually wants an on-chain euro or just talks about it at conferences remains the open question, but Quantoz is better positioned than most to find out.

deuro-deuro.title: The Oracle-Free Euro
deuro-deuro.text: Born from the same codebase as Frankencoin (ZCHF), dEURO takes the contrarian position that price oracles are a point of failure, not a feature — its CDP model uses internal auctions instead of external price feeds, a design that trades capital efficiency for resilience against oracle manipulation. The collateral is omnivorous: 40% WBTC, 25% WETH, 10% XAUT (tokenized gold), and smaller positions in USDC, DAI, UNI, and ZCHF, all valued through auction-based mechanisms on five chains. With governance fully transferred to token holders and no founder control over contracts, dEURO is genuinely decentralized in a euro stablecoin market where that word usually means 'we have a multisig' — one of only two decentralized euro stablecoins tracked by Pharos. MiCA's evolving stance on decentralized stablecoins could be either tailwind or existential threat, depending on whether European regulators view oracle-free design as innovation or evasion.

cetes-etherfuse.title: Three Counterparties, One Yield
cetes-etherfuse.text: CETES are Mexico's equivalent of Treasury bills — zero-coupon sovereign debt auctioned weekly by the Ministry of Finance — and Etherfuse has tokenized them into a NAV-accreting instrument backed 100% by CETES with INDEVAL custody, institutional-regulated oversight under CNBV/IPAB/CONDUSEF, and independent attestation. The BBB- sovereign rating is honest about where Mexico sits in the credit hierarchy — legitimate investment grade, but peso volatility means dollar-denominated exposure carries FX risk that doesn't appear in the APY headline. Deployed across four chains (Solana, Base, Polygon, Stellar), CETES tokens offer genuine access to Mexican sovereign debt for holders who can navigate the KYC-gated minting process. The yield is real and Banxico's rate cycle has kept CETES competitive globally — what the token hasn't resolved is which of its three dependencies (the peso, the sovereign, or the issuer) will cause the first inconvenient conversation.

zarp-zarp.title: The Rand's Digital Outpost
zarp-zarp.text: ZARP is backed 100% by ZAR in a treasury managed by Old Mutual Wealth — one of Africa's largest financial institutions — independently audited by Kempen, with institutional-regulated custody and an FSCA CASP license still pending. Deployed across Ethereum, Base, and Polygon, the infrastructure is sound but adoption has plateaued despite genuine demand for stable local-currency rails in a country where the rand regularly loses ground to the dollar. South African crypto regulation remains in perpetual draft mode, and ZARP's problem isn't credibility — it's relevance in a market that hasn't yet decided whether local-currency stablecoins solve a problem or just add complexity to existing USD pairs. For the small audience that needs on-chain ZAR exposure, ZARP is the only regulated option; for everyone else, USDC denominated in dollars remains simpler.

syrupusdc-maple.title: Institutional Lending, Vaulted
syrupusdc-maple.text: Maple Finance's syrupUSDC has become one of the largest yield-bearing stablecoins, channeling deposits into overcollateralized institutional loans. The ERC-4626 vault design makes it composable enough that Aave V3, Morpho, and Pendle have all integrated it — meaning your lending yield can itself be lent, borrowed against, or split into principal and yield tranches. Base expansion saw deposit caps fill immediately, suggesting institutional credit appetite exceeds available supply. The risk is the one that always haunts institutional credit: borrowers default, and 'overcollateralized' is only as good as the collateral's liquidation value in a downturn.

syrupusdt-maple.title: The Mirror Vault
syrupusdt-maple.text: Maple's USDT counterpart to syrupUSDC runs on identical mechanics — ERC-4626 vault, institutional borrower pool, overcollateralized credit lines — as the smaller sibling. The distinction matters less than it appears: both feed from the same Maple lending infrastructure, and yield differentials between the two are negligible. Ethereum-only deployment limits its DeFi composability compared to syrupUSDC's multi-chain reach, which may explain the size gap. For yield-seekers who prefer their stablecoin exposure in Tether rather than Circle, syrupUSDT is the vault; the economics are otherwise indistinguishable.

yousd-yield-optimizer.title: Fifty Strategies, One Token
yousd-yield-optimizer.text: YO Protocol's yoUSD automates what DeFi power users do manually — rebalancing USDC across 50+ yield sources on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and Unichain, ranked by risk scores with per-pool and per-protocol concentration caps. The track record of positive returns with zero negative months looks miraculous until you remember it was built during a bull market. Backed by Paradigm, Haun Ventures, and Coinbase Ventures, the deposits are modest but growing as the NAV appreciation model means your 'dollar' climbs steadily above $1 — stable in the sense that it never goes down, not that it stays at one. The real tension is philosophical: yoUSD is a sophisticated yield aggregator wearing a stablecoin's clothing, and the distinction matters when the bull market ends.

ustb-superstate.title: T-Bills Awaiting a Charter
ustb-superstate.text: Superstate's USTB has grown past $1.2 billion — 100% in short-duration T-bills and government agency securities (weighted average maturity ~28 days) held at BNY Mellon, sub-advised by Federated Hermes, earning a B safety grade at 72 with A+ in both resilience and dependency risk. Trading above $11 per share as a NAV-accreting token, USTB surprises anyone who expects a stablecoin dashboard entry to hold at $1 — it's a registered Reg D fund that happens to be an ERC-20, with Ernst & Young annual audits and Chronicle/Chainlink daily on-chain NAV transparency. A pending conversion to a Section 2(a)(7) registered money market fund would make it the first on-chain MMF with that SEC designation, unlocking institutional mandates currently blocked by fund policy. USTB's real significance is as yield-bearing infrastructure: it appears in the collateral stacks of frxUSD, Usual's USD0, and other stablecoins that want T-bill exposure without managing BNY Mellon custody relationships themselves.

ousg-ondo-finance.title: The Hundred-Dollar Stablecoin
ousg-ondo-finance.text: OUSG has grown past $700 million — 85% backed by BlackRock's BUIDL with 12% in BlackRock's FedFund and a 3% USDC liquidity buffer, making Ondo I LP BlackRock's largest single on-chain client and OUSG essentially a first-class derivative of BlackRock's tokenized money market presence. At over $114 per token with NAV appreciating daily, it is the least dollar-like entry on any stablecoin dashboard, which is why Ondo maintains rOUSG — a rebasing sibling that stays at $1 while OUSG accumulates. The SEC investigation closure in November 2025 without charges removed the key regulatory overhang, and the instant T+0 mint/redemption via OUSGInstantManager against USDC through BUIDL on-chain liquidity makes OUSG's exit infrastructure better than most tokenized funds. Restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers with on-chain KYC enforcement — tokens literally cannot transfer to non-whitelisted addresses — OUSG is less a stablecoin and more a tokenized mutual fund that borrowed the infrastructure.

cg-uscc.title: The Basis Trade, Institutionalized
cg-uscc.text: Calling USCC an RWA fund is technically accurate and culturally misleading — roughly half the portfolio consists of crypto cash-and-carry trades running long BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP spot against short futures, with T-bills and Superstate's own USTB providing the buffer. The structure targets T-bill-plus returns without directional crypto exposure, a delta-neutral thesis compelling enough that Aave V3 absorbed $123 million of it as collateral and Sky (MakerDAO) allocated another $100 million. Whether the basis trade delivers consistent premium over T-bills depends on futures markets staying in contango — which tends to be true in bull markets and suspiciously fragile when it matters most. USCC is Superstate's more interesting product: less obvious than a T-bill fund, and less obvious about what its risk profile actually looks like during a crypto deleveraging event.

mtbill-midas.title: Europe's T-Bill Token
mtbill-midas.text: mTBILL is Midas's compliance-first answer to the tokenized T-bill race: 97% in BlackRock's IB01 ETF with Swiss custody at Maerki Baumann, issued as a Liechtenstein FMA-approved MiFID II instrument — the exact bureaucratic architecture required to legally sell T-bill exposure to European professionals. Ankura Trust provides daily on-chain NAV attestations, and the RWA collateral quality with regulated-entity governance earns institutional credibility that most crypto-native tokenized treasury products lack. The 'not available to U.S. or UK retail persons' restriction is the mirror image of USTB and OUSG's American access gates, carving out a European institutional niche in a market dominated by U.S. issuers. Deployed across five chains, mTBILL functions as infrastructure in Midas's product stack and as stable collateral in third-party structured products — the European T-bill token for protocols that need regulatory certainty over DeFi composability.

wsrusd-reservoir.title: Ashes to APY
wsrusd-reservoir.text: Reservoir's rUSD processed $285M in redemptions 'without failure' in November 2025, then flatlined — the protocol's precise way of surviving a bank run while losing the patient. The reincarnation as wsrUSD is an ERC-4626 NAV vault backed by an unusually varied diet: 30% USDC, 25% USDT, 10% PYUSD, 5% GHO, 5% RLUSD, 5% USD1, plus strategy vaults and lending markets — seven upstream stablecoin dependencies curated by Steakhouse, Gauntlet, and other named managers. Credit Enforcer smart contracts enforce minimum 105% liquidity, solvency, and capital ratios before any leverage-increasing action, which is the kind of on-chain risk management that most yield protocols skip. Deployed across 15 chains with exotic collateral quality and multisig governance, wsrUSD's flexibility is genuine — but the seven-dependency architecture means the protocol's safety is a derivative of Circle, Tether, PayPal, Aave, Ripple, and World Liberty Financial simultaneously.

dusd-alto.title: The Isolated Vault Stablecoin
dusd-alto.text: Alto DUSD takes a kitchen-sink approach to collateral in isolated markets — 55% ETH and LSTs, 20% BTC tokens, 15% sUSDe, 5% Syrup USDC, and a 5M USDC PSM cap at 20 bps — so one bad collateral doesn't cascade into the rest. The 91-rated PSM backstop with permissionless atomic settlement is the structural highlight, and the perfect peg score with zero depeg events on $527K in circulation suggests the architecture works at micro-cap scale. DAO governance via ALTO token holders earns the decentralized classification, though the DEWS Watch band at 29 with 85% worst-pool stress signals that the on-chain market is thinner than the collateral diversity implies. The embedded Ethena dependency via sUSDe means DUSD inherits a slice of delta-neutral basis risk on top of its overcollateralization buffer — sophisticated risk engineering at a scale too small to stress-test.

dusd-dtrinity.title: The Borrower's Stablecoin
dusd-dtrinity.text: dUSD inverts the usual stablecoin economic model: instead of rewarding passive holders, it redirects float revenue from its sfrxUSD (42%), Curve AMO positions (35%), and multi-chain stablecoin reserves to subsidize borrowers through dLEND, its Aave V3 fork. The danger notice on the dashboard is unambiguous: dTRINITY was exploited on March 17, 2026, and dUSD should be considered at risk — Sonic deployment is paused, supply has contracted sharply, and the DEWS Alert band at 40 with a DEX price divergence of over 2,200 basis points confirms the severity. The 84-rated backstop with permissionless atomic redemption against a basket of stablecoins provides a structural floor, but the exploit has undermined the trust that the sophisticated AMO and SMO mechanisms were designed to build. Deployed across Ethereum, Fraxtal, Katana, and Sonic with chain-isolated reserves, dTRINITY built an elegant flywheel for a market that arrived at the worst possible time.

thbill-theo.title: Wrapping the Wrappers
thbill-theo.text: Theo's thBILL is 100% backed by tULTRA, which wraps Standard Chartered Libeara's ULTRA fund, which holds actual U.S. T-bills managed by Wellington Management — three entities and two wrappers between your token and a government bond. The Panama-incorporated structure with single-entity governance and no published proof of reserves contrasts sharply with the Ankura-attested mTBILL and E&Y-audited USTB it competes against, though Standard Chartered's custody and Wellington's management provide institutional ballast at the bottom of the stack. The RWA collateral quality and institutional-regulated custody classification acknowledge what's actually holding the assets, even if the wrapper depth adds layers of operational risk that the T-bill label might obscure. Deployed across four chains with KYC-gated minting and T+4 settlement on underlying collateral, thBILL has found its niche among institutional investors who want T-bill exposure without caring too much about how many wrappers sit between them and the bonds.

usdp-parallel.title: Fee Yield, No Tricks
usdp-parallel.text: Parallel's USDp is backed 50% by sfrxUSD and 50% by sUSDe — two yield-bearing stablecoins whose Parallelizer module adjusts minting and redemption fees dynamically to correct peg drift without oracles or liquidation cascades. The yield story is unusually honest: sUSDp distributes 70% of actual protocol fees from the Parallelizer, bridging, and flash loan modules, meaning yield tracks real usage rather than governance votes on a made-up rate. DAO governance across five chains with Bailsec audit and Certora formal verification suggest Mimo Labs built this for durability rather than speed, though the dependency on both Frax (sfrxUSD) and Ethena (sUSDe) means USDp inherits the risk profiles of two very different stablecoin architectures — one backed by BlackRock T-bills, the other by delta-neutral basis trades. The central tension is whether a fee-revenue yield model can remain attractive at small scale when it competes against synthetic dollar protocols running leveraged strategies at hundred-fold the size.

usdpt-western-union.title: Remittance Giant Meets Federal Charter
usdpt-western-union.text: Western Union moves $200B+ in cross-border remittances annually and has decided the next leg of that journey runs through Solana. USDPT is issued by Anchorage Digital Bank — the first federally chartered OCC crypto bank — with Western Union providing the distribution network spanning 200+ countries and half a million retail locations. The arrangement neatly sidesteps the "who regulates the issuer" question that haunts most stablecoin projects, since Anchorage already answers to the OCC. Whether a 170-year-old money transfer company can compete for on-chain liquidity against Circle and Tether remains the open question; the bet is that Western Union's physical footprint gives USDPT an on-ramp advantage nobody else can replicate.

roughrider-bnd.title: State-Owned Banking Goes On-Chain
roughrider-bnd.text: North Dakota's Bank of North Dakota — the only state-owned bank in the US — is building a wholesale stablecoin on Solana via Fiserv's infrastructure. Roughrider Coin is designed for bank-to-bank settlement, not consumer wallets, backed by USD reserves and 93-day Treasury notes. The pilot is pending ND Industrial Commission approval, making this one of the rare stablecoins whose launch date depends on a state government meeting agenda rather than a Discord vote. As the second US state stablecoin after Wyoming's FRNT, Roughrider represents an emerging pattern: state treasurers discovering that blockchain settlement is cheaper than correspondent banking, even if the branding choices remain firmly rooted in local pride.

fiusd-fiserv.title: The Payments Stack Play
fiusd-fiserv.text: Fiserv processes $2 trillion in payments annually for 6,000+ financial institutions and wants to make stablecoins just another rail in that plumbing. FIUSD is less a single stablecoin and more a platform: Paxos handles issuance, Circle provides ecosystem interop, PayPal enables interoperability, and Mastercard connects the payments network. The centralized-dependent classification captures this architecture accurately — FIUSD depends on an entire constellation of partners, any of which could become a bottleneck. The end-of-2025 launch target has quietly slipped into 2026 with no firm date, which either means careful regulatory preparation or the inherent difficulty of coordinating four major fintech companies on a shared timeline.

eur-qivalis.title: Twelve Banks, One Euro
eur-qivalis.text: Qivalis is the European banking establishment's answer to USDC and Tether: a MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin backed by a consortium of 12 major banks including BNP Paribas, ING, UniCredit, and BBVA. The reserve design — 40% bank deposits, 60% short-term eurozone government bonds — reads like a money market fund with a blockchain address. Qivalis B.V. is seeking an EMI license from the Dutch Central Bank, and no blockchain has been announced yet, which suggests the consortium is still negotiating whether they want Ethereum's liquidity or a permissioned chain's control. The central tension is whether twelve banks that compete fiercely in every other market can cooperate long enough to ship a product before Circle's EURC and SocGen's EURCV eat the entire MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin market.

pusd-polaris.title: Immutable CDP, Yield Included
pusd-polaris.text: Polaris Finance is building what its co-founders TokenBrice and 0xLuude call the successor to Liquity's ethos: a crypto-collateralized stablecoin on Ethereum with immutable core contracts, no admin keys, and no off-chain assets. pUSD is minted against pETH collateral via CDPs, and the yield-bearing angle comes from protocol revenue — borrowing interest, swap fees, conversion gains, and DEX fees — rather than from depositing reserves into Aave. The private testnet is live with a Q4 2026 target, which gives the team time to prove that you can ship immutability without sacrificing usability. For a market saturated with centralized fiat-backed tokens and yield products built on leverage, pUSD is a deliberate bet that there's still demand for the Liquity V1 philosophy, upgraded.

pgold-polaris.title: Synthetic Gold, No Vault Required
pgold-polaris.text: Polaris Gold shares infrastructure with its sibling pUSD but pegs to gold rather than the dollar — and critically, does so without any physical gold backing. Unlike XAUT or PAXG, which tokenize actual bars in Swiss vaults, pGOLD is a synthetic gold exposure minted from the same pETH collateral pool via CDPs on Ethereum. This makes it arguably more decentralized than any gold-pegged token on the market, at the cost of carrying all the risks of crypto collateral in a down market. Whether DeFi users want synthetic gold exposure from immutable contracts instead of custodied metal from Tether or Paxos is an experiment Polaris is willing to run.

usg-tangent.title: Productive Collateral, Dynamic Rates
usg-tangent.text: Tangent Finance is building USG as an over-collateralized CDP stablecoin that accepts productive DeFi collateral — Curve LP tokens, Pendle PTs, and Stake DAO positions — rather than raw ETH or stablecoins. The peg mechanism borrows from crvUSD’s playbook: instead of relying on redemptions, dynamic interest rates and a rewards deduction rate automatically increase when USG drifts below $1, incentivizing borrowers to repay. A yield-bearing sUSG vault (ERC-4626) lets holders capture protocol earnings passively, while TAN governance token holders direct the DAO and share revenue. The design bets that DeFi-native collateral can be more capital-efficient than traditional CDP models, though it inherits the composability risk of every protocol whose tokens it accepts.

klarnausd-klarna.title: Buy Now, Settle On-Chain Later
klarnausd-klarna.text: Klarna — the Swedish fintech with 114 million customers and $112B in annual GMV — is building a stablecoin via Stripe's Bridge infrastructure on the Tempo L1 (backed by a $500M Stripe/Paradigm raise). The initial use case is mundane by crypto standards but massive by payments standards: reducing Klarna's own cross-border settlement costs before expanding to consumer and merchant flows. Tempo testnet has been live since November 2025, though no official ticker has been disclosed. The interesting dynamic is that Klarna doesn't need external adoption for KlarnaUSD to succeed; its own payment volume is large enough to justify the infrastructure, making external DeFi liquidity a bonus rather than a requirement.

ussd-sonic-labs.title: Yield Without the Yield
ussd-sonic-labs.text: USSD is Sonic Labs' answer to why a fast EVM chain should depend on Circle and Tether to denominate everything — a permissionless, zero-fee stablecoin backed entirely by tokenized T-bills (BlackRock BUIDL, Superstate USTB, WisdomTree WTGXX) and built on Frax's frxUSD smart contract infrastructure. The design choice that distinguishes it from every other T-bill-backed stablecoin is also its most pointed: the Treasury yield flows to the Sonic ecosystem as buybacks and incentives, not to USSD holders, meaning every dollar sitting in USSD generates a return that benefits the protocol's treasury while the holder earns exactly $1. At roughly $2M in circulation at launch, this subsidy is trivial; at meaningful scale, it becomes a permanent off-balance-sheet revenue stream funded by users who chose the zero-yield option. The GENIUS Act-compatible framing and U.S. jurisdiction signal suggest Sonic Labs is building for a regulatory environment that hasn't fully arrived yet, which will look prescient or premature depending entirely on how fast Washington moves.

pgold-pleasing.title: Gold Without Receipts
pgold-pleasing.text: Pleasing Gold's PGOLD is backed 1:1 by LBMA-standard 99.99% physical gold at 1 troy ounce per token, deployed on Arbitrum and ApeChain — the same Pleasing International that issues PUSD, sharing infrastructure and the Hong Kong precious metals firm's physical gold corridor. The institutional-unregulated custody and absence of any proof of reserves or independent attestation make PGOLD the least transparent gold token on the dashboard, relying entirely on the issuer's claims without external verification.
