Whether a gold token without audited reserves can compete with PAXG's KPMG attestations and XAUT's BDO Italia audits depends on the holder's trust in the issuer rather than the metal itself. For Pleasing's existing gold corridor clients, PGOLD may serve as a convenient tokenized bridge; for everyone else, the lack of verifiable custody is a hard pass.

ggbr-goldfish-gold.title: The Paper Gold Token
ggbr-goldfish-gold.text: Goldfish Gold's GGBR represents 1/1000 of a troy ounce of gold per token, but unlike XAUT or PAXG, the backing is described as 'issuer balance-sheet gold exposure' rather than allocated physical bars — making it more a gold-tracking derivative than a tokenized commodity. The institutional-unregulated custody with no published proof of reserves, no independent attestation, and no disclosed jurisdiction means the entire trust chain runs through the Goldfish entity alone. Ethereum-only deployment with high-risk reserve classification reflects the Pharos assessment of what 'issuer-managed backing' means in practice: counterparty risk on the issuer rather than custody risk on the metal. In a tokenized gold market where PAXG offers individually serialized LBMA bars with KPMG attestations, GGBR's value proposition is hard to articulate beyond convenience.

axcnh-anchorx.title: The Offshore Yuan
axcnh-anchorx.text: AnchorX's AxCNH is a CNH-pegged stablecoin backed 100% by offshore Chinese yuan cash reserves at regulated financial institutions, issued under a Kazakhstan AFSA license — a jurisdiction that provides formal regulatory cover without the scrutiny of Hong Kong or Singapore. The institutional-unregulated custody classification and absence of proof of reserves or independent attestation mean the trust assumptions sit entirely with the AnchorX entity and its reported reserve figures. Deployed on two chains, AxCNH occupies an unusual niche: on-chain access to CNH exposure for a currency whose on-shore variant (CNY) is heavily capital-controlled by the People's Bank of China. Whether the offshore yuan stablecoin market is large enough to sustain a product without established exchange partnerships or DeFi integrations remains the open question.

idrt-rupiah-token.title: Indonesia's Digital Rupiah
idrt-rupiah-token.text: Rupiah Token's IDRT is backed 100% by Indonesian rupiah bank deposits held by PT Rupiah Token Indonesia, deployed natively across four chains — making it one of the more broadly distributed local-currency stablecoins despite operating with institutional-unregulated custody and no published proof of reserves. Indonesia's crypto market is among the largest in Southeast Asia, giving IDRT a genuine addressable market for IDR-denominated on-chain transactions and remittances, though the absence of specific regulatory licensing and independent reserve attestation limits the product to users who trust the issuer directly. The domestic regulatory landscape for stablecoins in Indonesia remains in development, meaning IDRT operates in a gray area where compliance is self-defined rather than externally enforced. For a country with genuine demand for affordable digital payment rails, IDRT's existence is more practical than innovative.

tryb-bilira.title: The Lira's Digital Outpost
tryb-bilira.text: BiLira's TRYB is a Turkish lira stablecoin backed 100% by TRY cash reserves, deployed natively across seven chains — the broadest distribution of any local-currency stablecoin in the Middle East and North Africa region. The institutional-unregulated custody and absence of proof of reserves or specific regulatory licensing reflect the current state of Turkish crypto regulation, where stablecoin issuance operates without a formal licensing framework. Turkey's double-digit inflation and persistent lira weakness create genuine demand for digital TRY rails — the same macro dynamics that make PikuDAO's USP profitable as a carry trade make TRYB useful as an on-ramp for Turkish crypto traders who need local-currency denomination. Seven-chain deployment suggests BiLira is building for breadth rather than depth, covering the chains where Turkish users actually trade.

ebusd-ebisu.title: Gold and Shorts on Plasma
ebusd-ebisu.text: Ebisu's ebUSD is a Liquity V2-style CDP with one of the most eclectic collateral baskets on the dashboard: 44% sUSDe (Ethena's yield-bearing token), 24% WBTC, 24% XAUt0 (Tether Gold on Plasma), 6% stcUSD, and 3% weETH — mixing synthetic dollars, wrapped Bitcoin, tokenized gold, and ETH LSTs into a single overcollateralized position. At barely $260K in market cap with 169 depeg events and persistent below-peg trading, ebUSD is too small to attract meaningful arbitrage, and the 78-rated collateral redemption backstop provides a structural floor that the thin secondary market can't close efficiently. Deployed natively on both Ethereum and Plasma with user-set interest rates, the Liquity V2 architecture is sound but the alt-LST-bridged collateral quality classification and DEWS Watch band at 35 reflect the risk profile of accepting tokenized gold and basis-trade derivatives as CDP backing. ebUSD is a micro-cap experiment in exotic collateral CDP design — interesting architecture on a scale too small to stress-test.

usdaf-asymmetry.title: Immutable Wrapper Stack
usdaf-asymmetry.text: Asymmetry's USDaf is a Liquity V2-style CDP with immutable contracts and A+ decentralization at 100 — one of only four stablecoins on the dashboard to achieve a perfect governance score. The collateral is a stack of yield-bearing stablecoin wrappers: 65% ysyBOLD (wrapped BOLD), 23% scrvUSD (wrapped crvUSD), 7% sUSDS, and smaller allocations to tBTC, sfrxUSD, and WBTC — meaning USDaf's peg depends on the peg of at least four upstream stablecoins. The C safety grade at 56 and only 45% time at peg tell the cost of this architecture: 102 depeg events on barely $1.4 million in circulation suggest the secondary market can't maintain the peg at this scale. The immutable-code governance is genuine and the 82-rated backstop provides structural support, but USDaf is currently a proof of concept for recursive decentralized stablecoin design rather than a liquid dollar.

usnd-nerite.title: tBTC's Immutable Dollar
usnd-nerite.text: Nerite's USND earns a B+ safety grade at 77 — the highest of any stablecoin under $5 million in market cap — with A+ in both decentralization and dependency risk, powered by immutable contracts on Arbitrum (a Stage 1 L2) accepting tBTC (86.5%), rETH, WETH, and wstETH as collateral. The A+ peg score at 87 and 82-rated backstop with permissionless collateral redemption validate the Liquity V2-style architecture, though the 172 depeg events and zero DEX liquidity reveal a product that is structurally sound but too small for secondary market trading. Separate Stability Pools per collateral type and user-set interest rates are sophisticated engineering that would serve a larger protocol well, deployed here on a product with barely $1.3 million in circulation. USND demonstrates that immutable governance, clean collateral, and a proven chain can produce an excellent safety profile even at micro-cap scale — the question is whether anyone will notice.

ftusd-flying-tulip.title: Cronje's Carry Trade
ftusd-flying-tulip.text: Andre Cronje's Flying Tulip raised $225 million to build a DeFi super-app, and the stablecoin at its center has attracted roughly $730K in circulation from 20 holders — a ratio of venture capital to actual usage that would make a Web2 startup blush. The delta-neutral pitch echoes Ethena's playbook but runs a domesticated version: USDC and USDT lent into Aave with borrowed native assets staked to generate carry, no CEX perpetuals in sight. Yield flows exclusively to sftUSD stakers while unstaked ftUSD proceeds feed the protocol treasury, a design that makes the base token a zero-yield stablecoin whose holders subsidize the protocol by default. Deployed on Ethereum and Sonic with single-entity governance, circuit breaker contracts, and full dependency on the two largest centralized stablecoins, ftUSD is less a standalone dollar and more an opt-in yield wrapper for USDC and USDT with extra steps.

brla-brla-digital.title: Brazil's Dollar Problem, Inverted
brla-brla-digital.text: Most stablecoins let emerging-market users escape their local currency into dollars. BRLA does the opposite: it tokenizes the Brazilian Real for on-chain use, backed by government bonds (titulos publicos) and BRL cash held by Avenia (formerly BRLA Digital), a Sao Paulo startup with $17M in Series A funding. Deployed natively on Polygon, Gnosis, Celo, and Moonbeam with no Ethereum presence, BRLA's chain footprint is unusual — Celo dominates with 76% of the ~$14.7M supply. The contract is upgradeable with full blacklisting via a COMPLIANCE_ROLE, governed by a single entity with no multisig or DAO, and proof-of-reserves attestations are self-reported on a Notion page. Yield variants (stBRLA, yBRLA) exist as separate tokens, positioning BRLA as infrastructure for BRL-denominated DeFi rather than just a remittance rail — though at sub-$15M market cap, the infrastructure is still looking for its builders.

rai-reflexer.title: The Anti-Stablecoin
rai-reflexer.text: RAI is the philosophical purist of stablecoins — a floating-rate, ETH-only, governance-minimized token that deliberately refuses to peg to any fiat currency. Its redemption price started at $3.14 (yes, pi) and drifts via a PID controller that adjusts interest rates to dampen market volatility, making it arguably the only stablecoin that is truly independent of the traditional financial system. Bluechip rates it B+ with a path to A- contingent on adding direct redemption, and the ~372% collateralization ratio demonstrates the protocol's conservative design. The governance minimization project reduced admin control significantly, though full immutability was never achieved — oracles and emergency parameters still require community maintenance. At ~$1.8M market cap across six chains, RAI has become a living museum piece: technically operational, intellectually significant, but with supply that has been slowly declining since DeFi summer. The contracts are a monument to what decentralization maximalism actually looks like when you build it — and what the market thinks that's worth.

silk-shade-protocol.title: The GDP-Weighted Privacy Dollar
silk-shade-protocol.text: SILK is what happens when you cross a stablecoin with a macro index fund and deploy it on a privacy chain. Pegged to a GDP-weighted basket of 20 global currencies — USD at 30%, CNY at 22%, EUR bloc at 14%, plus JPY, GBP, INR, and fourteen others — SILK doesn't track any single fiat currency, making it one of the most conceptually ambitious stablecoins tracked on Pharos. Built entirely on Secret Network using the SNIP-20 privacy token standard, every transaction is private by default with optional auditability via viewing keys. The stability architecture layers overcollateralized lending (ShadeLend), stablecoin redemption pools, bounded minting with DAO governance, and ShadeDAO bonds — a belt-and-suspenders approach deployed on a chain that most DeFi users have never touched. At ~$1.1M in circulation on a single unproven chain with no bridge to Ethereum, SILK is simultaneously the most interesting basket stablecoin in crypto and one of the hardest to actually acquire.

idrx-idrx.title: Indonesia's On-Chain Rupiah
idrx-idrx.text: IDRX competes with IDRT (Rupiah Token) for the Indonesian on-chain market, and the architectural contrast is telling: while IDRT is a simple ERC-20, IDRX deploys natively on seven chains (Polygon, Base, BSC, Klaytn, Gnosis, Etherlink, World Chain, plus Solana) with built-in bridge functions and a CertiK-audited upgradeable proxy. PT IDRX Indo Inovasi backs it 1:1 with IDR fiat and government bonds, though no independent auditor or specific custodian has been named publicly — the proof-of-reserves page exists but loads no documents. The contract includes explicit blacklisting (addBlackList, removeBlackList, destroyBlackFunds) controlled via a BLACKLIST_ROLE, which IDRX frames as law enforcement compliance. At ~$1.1M market cap denominated in a currency where 1 IDRX equals roughly $0.00006, the token deals in numbers that would make SHIB holders feel at home — the entire supply is 18.5 billion tokens. Whether Indonesia's crypto market needs two competing rupiah stablecoins or zero remains an open question.

mxnb-juno.title: Bitso's Quiet Peso Play
mxnb-juno.text: MXNB is the Mexican peso stablecoin from Juno, a product of Bitso — Latin America's largest crypto exchange — operated through a licensed IFPE (electronic payment funds institution) called NVIO PAGOS MEXICO. The contract architecture tells the whole story: it's a FiatTokenV2_2, the exact same Centre/Circle codebase that powers USDC, complete with blacklisting, pausing, and upgradeability. Deployed at the same address across Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Avalanche with quarterly attestation reports following International Valuation Standards, MXNB is a textbook regulated fiat stablecoin — just denominated in pesos instead of dollars. The transparency page reports reserves exceeding circulating supply at ~20.8M MXN, though with only 117 holders on Ethereum and a $1.1M USD market cap, the token's reach is currently closer to a pilot program than a payment network. Listed on Kraken and a handful of DEXes, MXNB is infrastructure waiting for a use case — or perhaps the use case waiting for Mexican DeFi to find it.

gbpm-mento.title: The CDP Inside the Reserve
gbpm-mento.text: GBPm marks Mento's architectural pivot from AMM-backed stablecoins to Liquity v2-style CDPs, and the design is a fascinating nested dependency. Unlike cUSD and cEUR, which mint directly against the Mento Reserve's multi-asset basket, GBPm is minted by depositing USDm (Mento's dollar stablecoin) as sole collateral into CDPs — meaning GBPm's peg depends on USDm's peg, which depends on the Reserve's solvency, which depends on CELO, stETH, sUSDS, EURC, and ETH prices. That's at least three layers of trust before you reach anything resembling a pound sterling. Deployed exclusively on Celo with bridged supply on Monad, the ~$627K market cap and oracle-enforced GBP/USD rates are protected by circuit breakers that halt trading during FX market closures. The Mento DAO governs via veMENTO with timelocks and watchdog veto, and the StableTokenV2 contract has no freeze or blacklist functions — genuinely permissionless at the token level, even if the collateral chain is anything but.

cjpy-yamato.title: ETH-Backed Yen, Quietly Running
cjpy-yamato.text: Yamato Protocol's CJPY is a JPY-pegged stablecoin built on a clean, ETH-only CDP model by DeFiGeek Community Japan — a DAO with no corporate entity behind it. The mechanism echoes Liquity's playbook: deposit ETH at 130% minimum collateralization, borrow CJPY with a one-time fee and no accruing interest, and face liquidation via a subrogation system that uses accumulated protocol fees to automatically repay underwater positions. The redemption floor — 1 CJPY always redeemable for 1 JPY worth of ETH from the riskiest pledge — provides a hard price floor without forced liquidation penalties. Deployed only on Ethereum with ~$1M in circulation, CJPY occupies the same philosophical space as RAI and LUSD: minimal governance, pure crypto collateral, no blacklisting, no upgradeability theater. The YMT governance token with veYMT vote-escrowed mechanics is planned but the protocol currently runs with DAO oversight via Snapshot. In a market where JPY stablecoins are dominated by centralized issuers like JPYC and GYEN, CJPY is the decentralized alternative that almost nobody uses — which, for its builders, may be precisely the point.
